releases.name: Cmod Progress Update - December 2025: What's next?
releases.body:
Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

I'm leaning on this being v13.2. A v14 Cmod should be more substantial. Ultimately I would like to overhaul how Containers are created, with a focus on something more aligned and user friendly like Gamehub, such as starting the app and choosing a Windows based executable directly in the UI, then auto creating or maintain a single container or edge case containers. This would work well with something like Per Game Fixes, or a standardized compatibility list like what's on Reddit.  

Lastly, I'm sorry I'm not good about addressing Github issues. I just have not had any time. However, it is all incredibly helpful for me; the time that I do have to spend on the next release and addressing what issues have been posted this past year (...and _cough_ Arc _cough_ raiding...). I am also looking forward to what Valve brings to the table with the Frame and it's ARM based Linux OS with Android app support. I imagine Proton is going to be getting some major improvements for ARM over the next year, so I don't see things slowing down much. Google seems to be walking back some of the unknown app restrictions they announced this year, so that's also good. Lots to look forward to. 

Stay Kazzy,
Goro Majima
_Majima Construction_

**Little update here... 03/06/2026** 
I pretty much finished my Joy-Con 2 / Nintendo Switch 2 Pro controller bluetooth driver/CLI tool for Linux systems, so I can get back to Winlator/PC Emulation on Android in general. 

You can check that out here: https://github.com/coffincolors/jc2mouse/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta1

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13.1.1
releases.body:
_Minor update v13.1.1 fixed custom icons, default renderer, and warning prompt handling on new installs_ 

------------------------------

-   **`evshim` Rewrite:** The entire controller shim (`libevshim.so`) has been rewritten, **completely eliminating the use of shared memory (`mmap`)**, resulting in a massive reduction in CPU overhead and a significant performance boost, especially on lower-end devices. Box64 3.2 and 3.6 are now compatible, and have been restored.

-   **ALSA-Reflector Improved** The pacer's ring buffer and reconnection logic have been refined, expect better performance and reliability.

-   **Universal CPU Overhead Reduction:** I've gone through the code to find and eliminate performance bottlenecks, once again, big thanks to @Pipetto-crypto as always for the guidance and his improvements to the Graphics Wrapper. 

### ✨ New Feature: VkBasalt Integration

-   **Per-Shortcut Sharpening & Effects:** Thanks to @Pipetto-crypto You can now enable VkBasalt on a per-shortcut basis to apply CAS and DLS to your games.

### 🐞 Stability & Bug Fixes:

This update includes a huge number of fixes for a smoother experience.

-   **Corrupted Shortcut Crash Fixed:** Implemented safety checks to prevent the app from crashing when parsing corrupted `.desktop` files.

-   **Proton & Frontend Fixes:** Resolved issues that caused crashes when launching the frontend or using XrActivity.

-   **Input Controls Fixed:** Corrected bugs with toggle switches and range buttons in the input controls overlay.

-   **Gyro Zeroing Improved:** The gyroscope now has better logic for finding its origin point, resulting in more responsive and accurate motion controls.

-   **Renderer Selection for DDraw:** Added a renderer selection option to fix black screens in older DDraw games, thanks to some last minute insight to **@Pipetto-Crypto**.

### ⚙️ Core & Asset Updates

-   **Proton 10 Support:** The codebase is now prepared for the next major Proton release. Stay tuned. (...and Wine 9.20)

-   **Updated Assets:** The default Box64, Proton packs, and other core assets have been updated with the latest fixes and improvements. Additional .wcp have been added to Contents: updated DXVK (+ Stripped, Sarek for lower end devices), updated VKD3D, and Turnip. Thank you @K11MCH1 for your excellent repository.

The list goes on actually. More planned as always- now get to testing! Spin up GTA IV and watch it fly! 🫡

-Alex

**WARNING: _Make new Containers_.** And if you were fast enough to get the apk within the first 5 minutes, please re-download it.

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13: The Controller Revolution is Here! (And much more...)
releases.body: The wait is over. After months of work the next major evolution of Winlator Cmod has arrived. I teased that a controller revolution was coming, but the reality is so much bigger. This isn't just an update; it's a top-to-bottom overhaul focused on bringing a native, seamless gaming experience to your device. This release is the culmination of a journey, and I'm proud to share it with you. ✨ What's New in Cmod v13 ✨ -------------------------- ### 🎮 The Controller Revolution: Native Gamepad Support is Here! The old input methods are gone (sorta), replaced by a completely new, from-the-ground-up controller implementation built on a native SDL2 backend. - **Native XInput & DInput Support:** No more switching settings per game! Controllers are now treated like real controllers. If it works on a PC, it should just work here. - **Multiplayer (Up to 4 Players!):** You heard that right. Connect up to four controllers and they will be properly recognized as Player 1, 2, 3, and 4. - **Vibration / Rumble:** Feel the action with full haptic feedback support. It can be toggled on or off. - **Advanced Motion Controls (Gyro):** A completely revamped and customizable gyroscope implementation. Map it to the left or right stick, fine-tune sensitivity, deadzone, and smoothing, and set an activation button. - **Turbo & Macros:** Set up autofire for any button (including triggers!) for each of your controllers. - **Virtual Gamepad Enhancements:** The on-screen controls are now more responsive than ever, with reactive visual feedback to show when a button is pressed. ### 🔊 ALSA-Reflector: The Unbreakable Audio Engine So- you're in a game, you connect your Bluetooth headphones or a phone call comes in, and the audio dies, forcing a restart. **Those days are over.** - **Introducing "ALSA-Reflector":** A new, optional audio driver that creates a virtual, unbreakable audio sink. It provides stable back-pressure to Wine, completely immune to Android's device changes. - **Seamless Recovery:** Real audio is mirrored to your hardware. If the connection breaks, the playback stream is automatically rebuilt in the background without interrupting the game's audio flow. The music never stops. (Well... it might, it's a work in progress!) ### 🚀 Core System & Proton Enhancements - **Bionic Native Libs:** Thanks to **@Pipetto-Crypto**, Winlator Cmod now uses native Bionic libraries. ### 🎨 UI & Quality-of-Life Tsunami - **Favorite Shortcut Launcher:** See that new star icon in the toolbar? Set your favorite game shortcut and launch it with a single tap from the main screen. - **"Disable Touchscreen Mouse" Option:** You can now completely disable the touchscreen as a mouse input device when using a virtual gamepad. - **Countless Fixes:** From custom shortcut icons and `.lnk` file parsing to a smarter app shutdown process and dozens of UI polish updates, nearly every corner of the app has been refined. The Journey & Thank You ----------------------- This release absolutely would not have been possible alone. - A massive thank you to **@Pipetto-crypto** for his phenomenal work on the graphics wrappers, Bionic native libraries, for taking the time to teach me the intricacies of compiling bionic native libraries, and for keeping the Cmod torch lit while I was on break. - To **@K11MCH1** for pushing me to learn how to compile Bionic libs in the first place and [his excellent videos,](https://www.youtube.com/@Zerokimchii) and the entire **EmuGear Discord community**: Your endless testing, feedback, bug reports, and encouragement were the fuel for this entire project. You guys make this all worth it. - And finally, a shout-out to my digital homies Gemini and GPT. For the countless late-night debugging sessions, untangling the multithreaded madness of the ALSA-Reflector, and providing the sanity checks I needed that kept this project on the rails---I genuinely couldn't have done it without you. This release is for all of you. Now, go play some games! *Alex* *ps: I'll write some helpful release notes tomorrow... time to rest haha...* **ALSO - IMPORTANT: CONTROLLERS REQUIRE NORMAL OR ESSENTIAL START-UP FOR SERVICES!** And box64 MUST be 3.7- it's a special patched version. Working on that next!

releases.name: MangoHud for Winlator Glibc - Fixed** GPU/CPU stats
releases.body:
Huge thanks to @hisham2630 of DarkOS for providing the source code for his implementation for certain hardware stats, which made this release possible (or significantly faster).

---

### Notes:
- **Battery Stats:** Requires root access and SELinux enforcement disabled. Other stats do not require root access.**
- **Limitations:** I/O RW is not implemented, and some features might not work on Android.
- **Fork:** Source code will be available on my MangoHub repo for contributions as soon as I prepare it.
- **Compatibility:** Currently works only with Glibc environments. **GPU Load on the Adreno a618 and a619 is currently not supported.
- **OpenGL:** _Can_ be enabled with `MANGOHUD_DLSYM` however, I cannot get it working in my testing. If you get different results, let me know. 
---

### Installation Instructions:

1. Set the following environment variables in your Winlator container settings:
   - `MANGOHUD=1`
   - _Optionally_: `MANGOHUD_CONFIG=engine_version,gpu_temp,fps,frametime,ram,vulkan_driver,arch`
     *(You can customize these. See [MangoHud Parameters](https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud))*.

2. Download and unzip `Winlator_Mangohud_Glibc_Release.zip` somewhere on your storage.

3. Launch a _Glibc_ 😉 container, and Run the provided `install_mangohud.bat`:
   - This will merge the `usr` directory with the existing `usr` directory in Wine's Z: drive.

4. Alternatively:
   - Copy the `usr` directory manually to your Wine Z:/ drive and merge it.

5. You're all set! Launch your Wine application to enjoy MangoHud overlays.

This will be included by default in the next Winlator Cmod release.

---

- Fast forward almost a year and a half later—with over 1,100 pull requests—I’ve managed to update this codebase from Dolphin 5.0-18205 (December 2022) all the way to Dolphin 2407 (July 2024). ### **Changelog for v2.3.000 (from v2.2.110)**

- Extensive code refactors including a major overhaul of the graphics pipeline
- Graphics pipeline code revision - removed obsolete MMJR2-specific hacks, that are no longer needed
- Revised and improved Asset Loader
- Updated external components like SDL, Cubeb, mGBA, fmt, etc.
- Updated NDK to v25.2.9519653
- Updated Android libraries, now targeting Java 17
- Many JIT optimizations
- Minor updates to the Vulkan backend
- Optimized Vertex Loader
- Updated GameINI database
- Fixed Fast Forward hotkey
- Added support for WiiConnect24 via WiiLink
- Added support for Color Space Correction
- Leveraged LZ4 algorithm for faster savestate decompression
- Updated and fixed multiple instances of partially synced code across the project

### **Missing features - these features from Dolphin Official are not implemented**

- Android Input Overhaul and subsequent changes to Input and TAS handling
- Custom GPU driver support
- Skylanders portal and Infinity base support
- Gamma correction

**This codebase is roughly equivalent to the Official Dolphin dev build 5.0-20223 (Oct 15, 2023).**

### General information
This release includes over 7 months' worth of code changes ported from Dolphin Official since v2.2.110, and more than 3 months since the last beta. I’ve tested it extensively, but as always, your mileage may vary. 🤷‍♂️ I upgraded my RP3+ to a Retroid Pocket 4 Pro and performed most of the testing on this device.

Android developers willing to help are always welcome! 

### Caution

- Save States from v2.2.110, v2.3.000-rc1, and v2.3.000-rc2 are NOT compatible with this release. Be sure to have in-game saves before updating!
- Due to the graphics pipeline changes, this build bumps the shader cache UID version. Shaders will need to be cached and built from scratch, so expect some initial shader compilation stutter.

### Known Issues

The UI in the Cheats section is broken when you try to delete multiple items in a row. This bug is present to this day in Dolphin Official. Just delete a few items, exit the cheats window, and return back.

As always, have fun and happy gaming ✌️

Welcome to a huge update for XoDos! This release packs a massive punch with refinements across the entire app, from a polished UI to powerful new under-the-hood features for both Wine and the Proot environment. Get ready for a smoother, more compatible, and more controllable experience.

✨** What's New in the App?**

· 🎨 Updated & Fixed App UI: A refreshed and more stable user interface for a better overall experience.
· ⚙️ New Quick-Settings Menu: Added new settings for instant access to install DXVK/D3D and drivers for Wine anywhere, anytime! No more complicated commands.
· 🚀 Termux-X11 Performance Boost: Updated to the latest official code! Now featuring hardware buffer support for significantly improved performance and smoothness.
· 📋 Restored Start Menu & Widgets: The convenient start menu is back! Plus, we've added handy Termux widgets for quicker access.
· 🍷 Wine Bionic Updated: Upgraded to Wine 10.0-rc3 x86_64 for much better application and game compatibility.
· 🔧 Fixed Desktop Scripts: Fixed scripts for both Wine Glibc and Bionic. You can now properly stop the desktop from the settings with the "Stop Desktop" button.
· 🖥️ Fixed Native Desktop Launcher: Resolved a bug in the hardware acceleration mode selector that was incorrectly choosing VIRGL mode for Linux apps.
· 🐛 Fixed Proot Desktop Script: The script for launching the Proot desktop has been fixed and stabilized.
· 🖱️ Fixed External Mouse Support: Improved the mouse capturing method for a more reliable external mouse experience.

---

🪄 What's New in the Proot System?

The integrated Proot environment has received a massive upgrade, turning it into a powerhouse for Windows applications.

· 🍷 Wine 9.17: Added the latest and greatest Wine version (9.17) for cutting-edge support.
· 🤖 New Box64 Integration: Added brand-new Box64 for vastly improved x86_64 Windows game and application support on ARM64 devices!
· 🎯 Experimental Turnip Drivers: Added new Turnip drivers (Mesa RadV). They can be installed via .bat files for now. Once stable, they will be integrated into the quick-settings menu just like Bionic and Glibc.
· ⚡ DXVK & Wined3D Installation: Added the ability to install DXVK and Wined3D directly from .bat files inside the Proot environment, same as the drivers.
· 📊 MS Office Installation Fixed: MS Office can now be installed and fixed anytime directly from the desktop.
· 🎮 Updated OpenGL/Zink: Updated and fixed OpenGL and Zink implementations for better graphics rendering.
· 🔬 Beta VIRGL Drivers: Added VIRGL drivers for both Wine and Linux applications (marked as beta for now).
· ...and more! Various under-the-hood tweaks and fixes for a rock-solid experience.

releases.name: Mainline Turnip v32
releases.body:
Mainline Turnip Vulkan V32
Built from: https://github.com/whitebelyash/mesa-unified (turnip/gen8 branch). Took a while.  

I didn't test this this much. Contact me on MojoLauncher.en (#offtopic-non-help, requires Community role) or EmuCore discord if there are any issues.


>[!WARNING]
> Please don't report issues to Mesa, PLEASE
          
Supported GPUs:
* Adreno 8XX Family: 840, 830, 829, 825, 812, 810
* Adreno 7XX Family: any GPU supported by the upstream Turnip + 710/720/722 (unstable, sysmem only). Thanks, https://github.com/Vauzi-17/710.  
(Upstream has more fixes, so check it too)
* Adreno 6XX Family: any GPU supported by the upstream Turnip


Notes:
* Disable DXVK_HUD if you see weird black artifacts
* Apparently there are swizzling glitches in Eden & maybe other emulators, try increasing render scale(?)
* Some games may require AMD/NVIDIA GPU to run and refuse to start on Qualcomm or block some features. I've included a patch to spoof as Steam Deck - use `TU_DEBUG=deck_emu`
* GMEM rendering produces glitchy picture on A830 (write page faults), disable it with `TU_DEBUG=sysmem`. It's pretty much useless for PC emulation anyway.

Changes
* Upstream rebase
* Rebase build fixes

That's it for now. For now.

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1
releases.body:
# Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1

A fixes-and-polish update to 1.2.

## ⚠️ Reinstall Required!
Uninstall the old version and install 1.2.1 fresh. Back up your game saves first (Save Manager, or copy them out of your container). Containers made on 1.2 are not carried over.

## Fixes for 1.2 user reports
- Fixed a reboot on some MediaTek Mali phones (JM Mali).
- Fixed a crash when opening a shortcut.
- Fixed the controller binding editor.
- Fixed the stutter when holding D-pad right.
- Fixed File Manager not opening (it needed `libcdio.dll`), and File Manager hanging on x86_64 Wine (replaced with Bannerlator's newer `wfm.exe` / `winhandler.exe`).

## Graphics and performance
- **Fullscreen modes:** Fit, Stretch, Fill and Integer, plus screen alignment (Center, Top, Bottom half), set per container or per game and changeable live in Display & Session.
- **EGL stripes fixed:** CPU writes into the window buffer are flushed per X batch.
- **ZeroFG:** the default multiplier is capped at the display refresh rate (40 fps on a 60 Hz screen now gives 1.5x instead of 2x with dropped frames).
- **Gladio:** refuses OpenGL contexts above 3.3 again; libGL stripped of debug info (1.48 MB to 488 KB).
- **D7VK** is its own content type, with a DDraw wrapper option.

## Wine, Proton and containers
- Wine/Proton setup follows Bannerlator: each container uses its own prefix only, layer DLLs are copied and refreshed, `EnableLUA=0`, the prefix is updated before a session, and no always-present `event0`.
- The default container pattern is updated: AIO and controller tests, Pale Moon, libcdio, winlauncher, our install scripts and 7z.
- **Contents:** badges for DXVK/VKD3D (arm64ec or x86), FEXCore (unixlib or DLL), Box64/WOWBox64 and NTSync; same-named entries labelled by release folder; Wine/Proton without arm64ec in the name are marked x86_64; unknown content types (Turnip/Rutabaga driver zips) are no longer listed as Wine.

## Controls
- **Simulate touch screen** (from brunodev85), in Settings > Mouse under Cursor Speed: a tap clicks where you touch, and a one-finger drag moves the cursor there.

## Log Manager (new)
Modelled on Bannerlator, in our UI:
- Per-game log folders with run history.
- Wine debug with channels, Box64/FEXCore, DXVK/VKD3D, logcat, crash reports and exit reasons.
- A viewer with find, wrap, copy and share, and View logs on each shortcut.
- A master Logs switch: off records nothing anywhere.
- It lives in Settings > Advanced.

## Interface
- Side menu follows every theme preset, with the version under the title, an inset selected pill and compact rows.
- Containers screen: cards on the preset surface, with arch chip, Wine/Proton version and screen size.
- Community Configs: same-named games merged (counts summed, configs of all ids listed), and Mali / Adreno badges spelled out.

## Credits
Thank you to the projects and people whose work this update builds on:
- **brunodev85 (Bruno):** Winlator and Gladio. *Simulate touch screen* (Move Cursor to Touchpoint) comes from his Winlator, and Gladio's OpenGL 3.3 limit follows his original.
- **The412Banner / Bannerlator:** the newer File Manager (`wfm.exe`) and `winhandler.exe`, the container pattern, the Wine/Proton prefix setup, fullscreen modes and screen alignment, and the model for our Log Manager.
- **Pipetto-crypto:** the native EGL renderer; the window-buffer write flush follows his lock/write/unlock.
- Everyone credited in the [1.2 release](https://github.com/GunaCharanTeja/WinlatorMali/releases/tag/bionic-mali-1.2): Bruno (`brunodev85`), Pipetto-crypto, leegao, stevenmxz, vivsi1, Noysz, The412Banner / BannerHub, longjunyu2, hy300leosquizz-ctrl and willfaust (Madeira).
## Flavors
- **Standard** `com.winlator.mali`: recommended.
- **Ludashi** `com.ludashi.benchmark`
- **AnTuTu** `com.antutu.ABenchMark`

Contact: [Telegram group](https://t.me/+RDjo9_ORqXgwODc1) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/gunacharanteja)

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2
releases.body:
Winlator Mali Bionic v1.2 Winlator Mali Bionic v1.2 is a major architectural overhaul over v1.1, introducing a native EGL rendering engine, ZeroFG Vulkan compute frame interpolation, a redesigned UI with Madeira Liquid Glass touch controls, two selectable BCn layers, hardware performance tools, kernel-direct telemetry, and a cloud-powered community configuration ecosystem. ⚠️ Reinstall Required!
🖥️ Native EGL Rendering Engine & Gladio Integration
  • High-Performance Native EGL Architecture: Migrated from the legacy v1.1 rendering stack (GLRenderer, DisplayX, VirGL, blit_converter, and Java EffectComposer) to Pipetto-crypto's native C++ EGL renderer at app/src/main/cpp/winlator/renderer/egl.cpp.
  • Elimination of Legacy Overhead: Removed the legacy DisplayX layer (displayx.cpp, DisplayXView), VirGL (VirGLRendererComponent), and blit_converter.cpp, eliminating over 3,500 lines of redundant CPU blit and synchronization code.
  • Gladio Native OpenGL Engine: Integrated the native Bionic libGL.so.1.7.0 Gladio engine with cached blit targets and native synchronization fences.
  • Cross-API Zero-Copy Hardware Buffer Sharing: Shares OpenGL/EGL frames with a Vulkan compute device through Android Hardware Buffers (AHardwareBuffer), using native Linux sync files for frame interpolation.
  • Modern X Server Infrastructure: Added support for RandR (RandrExtension), Present 1.2 (PresentConfigureNotify), and ReparentNotify, with enhanced DRI3 event routing.
  • Unified Graphics Enhancements UI: Combined PostFX, Frame Generation, and FPS Limiter settings into GraphicsEnhancementsDialog.
  • Native C++ PostFX Pipeline: Replaced Java-based compositing with an optimized C++ shader pipeline.
Upscalers
  • AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR 1.0)
  • Qualcomm Snapdragon Game Super Resolution (SGSR)
  • Lanczos2
Shaders & Filters
  • Fake HDR
  • FXAA
  • CRT
  • NTSC
  • Toon
  • Sharpening
  • Ludashi Color Boost
⚡ ZeroFG Frame Generation
  • Legacy APEX / MCFI Removed: Removed the legacy APEX frame generation engine and its shader pipelines.
  • ZeroFG Compute Interpolation Core: Integrated the custom Vulkan compute frame interpolation engine (zerofg), optimized for ARM Mali tile-based GPU architectures.
  • Custom Mali-Tuned Passes: Added rc3_mali_d2, rc3_mali_d4, rc3_mali_d5a, and rc3_mali_d5b.
  • Motion Estimation: Includes subgroup motion estimation, optical flow lattice tracking, camera motion estimation, and split resolve passes.
  • Intermediate Frame Generation: Synthesizes intermediate frames to improve perceived smoothness.
  • Fractional Multipliers: Supports fractional frame generation multipliers with display refresh-rate synchronization, isolated to the game rendering window.
🎨 Complete UI Revamp & Modernization
  • Full Theme Engine: Added ThemeManager with custom dark and light themes and customizable accent colors through CustomThemeDialog.
  • Tabbed Settings Architecture: Reorganized global settings into six categories: Appearance, Emulation, Input & Display, Storage & Audio, Performance, and Advanced.
  • Inter Typography: Standardized UI controls and dialogs on Inter SemiBold (Inter.ttf), licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
  • Card-Based Visual Layouts: Redesigned Adrenotools, Save Manager, Input Controls, Manage Graphics Drivers, and shortcut lists with card containers, rounded edges, and soft shadows.
  • Official Vector Component Logos: Added official vector logos for Wine, Box64, FEXCore, DXVK, VKD3D, and Proton.
  • Overhauled About Section: Added architecture highlights, developer credits, and clickable open-source licenses.
  • Fullscreen Cinematic Preloader: Added custom 16:9 SteamGridDB hero banners with a loading scrim and dynamic status messages, including "Waiting for the game to render…".
🚀 Hardware Optimization & Performance Suite
  • Adrenotools on Unsupported Devices: Added the show_adrenotools_unsupported option, allowing users on Mali and other non-Qualcomm devices to access Adreno Tools and manage custom graphics driver layers.
  • Dedicated In-Game Performance Dialog: Added access to hardware performance options during gameplay.
  • Game Mode Signal: Signals Android Game Mode for system prioritization.
  • Thread Priority: Adjusts game and translation thread scheduling priorities.
  • Big Cores Affinity: Pins execution threads to high-performance CPU cores.
  • Sustained Performance Mode: Requests sustained performance to help reduce aggressive thermal clock throttling.
  • Samsung Game SDK / SPerf Boost: Integrates Samsung Game SDK / SPerf functionality for supported Samsung devices.
  • RAM Booster (LMK Trigger): Added seven memory-management profiles: Smart Auto, Low, Medium, High, Aggressive, Max, and Manual.
  • Custom Memory Thresholds: Added configurable Crisis and Pre-Crisis thresholds with toast notifications.
  • PulseAudio-GN Audio Driver: Added the GameNative PulseAudio driver alongside ALSA and standard PulseAudio.
  • Custom FPS Limiter: Added the ability to set an arbitrary target frame rate.
🎮 On-Screen Controls & Input Engine Overhaul
  • Madeira Liquid Glass Touch Style: Introduced a new default WinMali touch-control style with light-catching rims, lens edges, highlights, and subtle shadows.
  • Xbox & PlayStation Visual Profiles: Added cached bitmap controller styles for improved visibility.
  • High-Visibility Minimum Alpha: Maintains a minimum opacity of 55% for touch controls.
  • Steam Deck-Style Radial Action Wheels: Added an eight-slice pie menu activated by holding a trigger, with analog-stick and touch-drag navigation, custom slice icons, and vibration confirmation.
  • Live In-Game Controls Editor: Reposition, resize, and rebind buttons through a transparent overlay without pausing or exiting the game.
  • Four-Player Multi-Controller Slots: Added manual slot assignment, per-player deadzones, and LED color mapping.
  • Universal Icon Packs: Added Bannerlator .icpx custom icon packs, Base64-embedded profiles, and InputBridge .ibp profile translation.
  • High-Resolution Icon Rendering: Supports 512 × 512 anti-aliased icon rendering.
  • Precision Gyroscope Subsystem: Added motion-to-aim controls with independent X/Y sensitivity, axis inversion (gyroInvertX, gyroInvertY), dynamic acceleration curves, and steering support.
🧱 Dual BCn Layers — Current & LegacyWinlator Mali Bionic v1.2 introduces two selectable BCn layers, available directly through BCn Config.

⚡ Current BCn Layer

  • Faster Processing Speeds: Faster processing than the legacy BCn layer.
  • Lower Memory Usage: Uses less memory than the legacy layer.
  • Native BCn-Equivalent Memory Usage: Memory consumption is exactly the same as native BCn support.
  • Optimized Texture Handling: Focuses on performance and memory efficiency.

🔄 Legacy BCn Layer

  • Established Transcoding Implementation: Retains the existing BCn texture-transcoding approach.
  • Selectable Output Formats: Transcodes BCn textures into the user-selected format.
  • Supported Formats: ASTC, ETC2, and ETC1.

⚙️ Configuration

Choose your preferred layer directly in BCn Config.
  • Current: Faster processing, lower memory usage, and memory consumption exactly matching native BCn support.
  • Legacy: Configurable texture transcoding to ASTC, ETC2, or ETC1.
📊 Kernel-Direct Telemetry HUD (Winlator HUD)
  • Real Mali GPU Load & Clocks: Queries Linux kernel sysfs nodes, including /sys/class/misc/mali0/device/utilization and /sys/class/devfreq/.../cur_freq, to report GPU utilization and operating frequency.
  • Accurate CPU Usage: Calculates per-process CPU activity using /proc/stat and process cgroup threads.
  • Battery Wattage: Displays live battery discharge power in watts using hardware voltage and current readings.
  • Thermal & Frametime Metrics: Adds a real-time frametime histogram, 1% and 0.1% lows, and thermal mitigation status.
  • Layer-Free Rendering: Renders HUD elements without intermediate composition layers for sharp text at different display scales.
🔌 USB Gamepad Attachment & Dual Rumble
  • Direct USB HID Host Mode: Added USB OTG gamepad support with device filtering through usb_device_filter.xml.
  • Persistent USB Permissions: Improved permission handling across supported device reconnects.
  • Dual-Motor Haptic Rumble: Added force feedback for compatible Xbox, PlayStation DualShock/DualSense, and X-Input gamepads.
  • Vibration Test & Calibration: Added VibrationTestDialog with independent left heavy motor, right light motor, both-motor, and pulse-pattern tests.
  • Full D-Pad / Controller UI Navigation: Added physical controller navigation throughout dialogs, menus, and side drawers.
☁️ Community Configs & Cloud Ecosystem
  • Cloudflare Workers & KV Backend: Added community configuration feedback with Helpful (👍) and Didn't Work (👎) ratings.
  • Anonymous Voting: Uses persistent anonymous voter UUIDs and anti-spam cooldowns.
  • Automated GPU Badges: Automatically detects and tags configurations as Mali- or Adreno-compatible.
  • Unbundled Wine Downloader: Automatically downloads and installs missing Wine/Proton packages when importing community configurations.
💾 SteamGridDB Hero Art & Game Save Manager
  • 16:9 Widescreen Hero Banners: Automatically fetches high-resolution game banners from SteamGridDB, with an interactive artwork selector.
  • Universal Save Manager: Scans and restores game saves from common locations.
  • Supported Save Locations: AppData, Saved Games, Documents, Steam/userdata, and supported game-specific folders, including Goldberg, CODEX, FLT, EMPRESS, and RUNE.
  • Windows PE Detection: Extracts executable version information using PEParser, extracts embedded icons, and tracks playtime.
🛠️ Bug Fixes, Stability & Refinements
  • File Manager Crash: Fixed a crash when opening the integrated File Manager.
  • Storage Information Dialog: Fixed incorrect 0% usage calculations and a clipped circular progress indicator.
  • USB Controller Reconnection: Improved background/resume handling to prevent USB device handles from remaining locked.
  • Android Permissions: Fixed Android 12+ immutable permission flags.
  • Touch & Mouse Pointers: Fixed cursor trapping in screen corners caused by NaN cursor speeds and corrected touch-event forwarding.
  • Touchscreen & Radial Wheel: Fixed default touch-control disabling and conflicts between touch controls and radial-wheel triggers.
  • Controls Profile Reset: Made profile resets non-destructive, preserving custom icons, button placements, and imported .icp/.icpx assets.
  • Icon Rendering Pipeline: Fixed integer ID overflow, restored 100% opacity for custom imported assets, and improved AndroidSVG vector parsing.
  • Audio Routing: Fixed PulseAudio-GN identifier mismatches and library loader paths.
  • Multiplayer LAN: Fixed local IP detection for LAN multiplayer.
  • Container Environment Variables: Ensured default environment-variable migrations run only once, allowing user deletions and custom edits to persist.

releases.body:
Winlator Mali Bionic v1.1

🚀 New Features

---

🎮 Unreal Engine 3 Preset

- Added a dedicated Unreal Engine 3 preset.
- Tested with X-Men Origins: Wolverine for improved compatibility and performance.

---

⚙️ Hybrid x86 FEXCore

- Added a custom Hybrid x86 FEXCore.

What does it do?

- Improves compatibility while maintaining high performance.
- Fixes physics issues in supported games that normally require x86 Reduced Precision to be completely disabled.

Why is it better?

Normally, disabling x86 Reduced Precision forces software emulation for all x86 code, which can significantly reduce performance.

Hybrid x86 only uses software emulation where it is actually needed (such as physics calculations), while allowing the rest of the game to run natively for much better performance.

Tested Games

- ✅ Assassin's Creed Revelations – Physics issues fixed while using the Performance preset.
- ✅ Assassin's Creed Brotherhood – Physics issues fixed while using the Performance preset.
- ⚠️ Assassin's Creed III – Still requires x86 Reduced Precision to be fully disabled.

«Note: Hybrid x86 improves compatibility for many games but is not a universal solution.»

---

⚡ Improvements

- Improved ImageFS and Wine installation speeds by replacing TZST packages, resulting in significantly faster extraction and setup times.
- Updated various DXVK, Box64, FEX, Vulkan Wrappers, and compatibility presets.
- Improved overall compatibility, stability, and performance across supported games.

X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 1
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 1

This hotfix improves driver management and restores Android shortcuts, with a new way to refresh global settings without reinstalling the app.

## Vulkan drivers

- Fixed downloads from driver catalogs that had stopped working.
- Improved package checks and clearer messages for unsupported or incompatible driver packages.
- Driver compatibility still depends on the device and package; this update does not make every custom driver compatible with every device.

## Android shortcuts

- Fixed game shortcuts not being created from the game menu.
- Fixed copying game launch links from the same menu.
- Android still asks for confirmation before adding a shortcut to the Home screen.

## Reset global settings

- Added a circular-arrow button beside the Settings search bar to restore global cvars to the current code defaults.
- A confirmation explains what will be reset. Afterward, you can immediately rerun initial setup to choose the app and console languages and review console options.
- Per-game overrides, storage locations, library, profiles, saves, drivers and patch selections are preserved.
- No settings are reset automatically when updating. The reset is optional and takes effect the next time a game starts.

## Updating

- Update in place; there is no need to uninstall or delete data.
- Verified on Odin 2. Wider device and driver coverage remains limited.
- TV mode and synchronized player profiles remain highly experimental and may still have issues.
- X360 Companion is unchanged.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5

This update focuses on more reliable profile and save imports, together with improvements to graphics processing and performance.

## Profiles and saved games

- Improved import reliability, including backups created with earlier versions of X360 Mobile.
- Clearer previews and confirmation before replacing existing profile or saved-game data.
- Stronger checks and recovery when an import is cancelled or interrupted, helping protect existing data.
- Preserves the original profile and saved-game ownership when restoring backups.

## Graphics and performance

- Improved graphics-work scheduling and reduced avoidable processing overhead.
- Added and refined graphics optimizations, evaluated using **GTA IV on Odin 2**.
- Further improvements to graphics-resource handling and pipeline reliability.

Two graphics optimizations are now **enabled by default**. Previously saved choices to disable them, including per-game overrides, continue to be respected. Both options can still be turned off.

Performance gains depend on the game, device, driver and settings. Other experimental graphics optimizations remain **opt-in**. Testing across other games and GPU families is still limited.

## Updating

- Existing installations can update in place and keep their games, settings, profiles and saves. There is no need to uninstall first.
- Existing preferences and per-game overrides are preserved.
- TV mode and synchronized player profiles remain highly experimental and may still have issues.
- X360 Companion is unchanged.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 2
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 2

This update brings general correctness, graphics, stability and efficiency improvements, developed and evaluated using **Split/Second** as a reference game. These are improvements to the emulator itself rather than fixes restricted to one title. Other games may also benefit, but broader compatibility and performance testing is still limited.

## Improvements

- Improved handling of demanding graphics workloads and reduced avoidable processing overhead.
- Corrected visual consistency and resource-handling issues, including an issue affecting frame interpolation.
- Improved the reliability of the touch-control layout editor.
- Added optional independent auto-hide for the Menu button.
- Reorganized Settings with fewer main categories and clearer access to game content, patches and advanced tools.

## Split/Second: still experimental

On the tested **Snapdragon 8 Gen 2** setup, Split/Second currently fluctuates around **8–18 FPS**, depending on the scene and the selected experimental settings. The game **still requires extensive further work to become playable on this SoC**. Occasional pauses and remaining graphical issues are still under investigation.

The experimental per-game options used for these tests remain **opt-in**; this update does not enable them globally. Results on other devices, drivers and games have not been widely verified.

## Updating

- Public version **0.6.4 Hotfix 2**, build **60411113**. Existing installations can update in place and keep their games, settings and saves.
- Includes the fixes from Hotfix 1. TV mode and synchronized player profiles remain highly experimental.
- X360 Companion is unchanged.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 1
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 1

This maintenance update fixes game-folder import and unnecessary temporary game copies, and adds a way to silence repeated external-display prompts.

## Fixes

- **Game folders on fresh installations:** fixed a folder-import path that could report “No XEX, ELF, ISO, ZAR or STFS/GOD titles found” even when the selected folder contained supported games. Android can expose different file lists depending on the storage permissions granted; folder import now uses the authorized access method instead of treating an incomplete local listing as an empty folder.
- **Direct ISO/ZAR access:** supported images exposed by Android's file picker can now be read directly when the storage provider supports it. Previously, the absence of a normal filesystem path could trigger an unnecessary full temporary copy even though the image was readable. Providers that only offer streams or partial files may still require the explicit copy option.
- **Repeated TV-mode prompts:** added a persistent option to disable automatic external-display prompts, plus “Don't ask again” in the prompt itself. This gives users a way to stop repeated notices when Android incorrectly reports an external screen. Manual TV-mode and display selection remain available in Settings → Interface → Displays and TV.

## Updating

- Public version **0.6.4**, build **60411108**. Existing installations can update in place and keep their data.
- If a folder failed to import previously, select it again after updating. All-files access remains available through Android's permission screen.
- TV mode and synchronized player profiles remain highly experimental.
- Includes the features and improvements from the [original 0.6.4 release](https://github.com/Ashnar2602/X360-Mobile---OFFICIAL/releases/tag/v0.6.4%2Bf398ad183).

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.4
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.4

This update moves X360 Mobile to a newer Xenia Edge core, with a refreshed Android interface, new ways to play and share compatibility results, and further work on game compatibility and performance.

## New features

- Optional frame interpolation for smoother displayed motion, with automatic and per-game controls.
- Experimental TV mode with larger game covers, top-tab controller navigation and external-display selection.
- X360 Mobile Live Lobbies for supported System Link games: direct LAN/Internet connections, public or friends-only rooms, optional passwords, invitations, chat, friend requests and friend presence. Two-console co-op has been checked in Gears of War.
- Experimental synchronized player profiles using X360 Mobile website accounts, with achievement and Gamerscore synchronization across devices.
- Automatic discovery of games added to registered library folders, without requiring another manual scan.
- Local autocomplete suggestions in the Xbox-style keyboard for installed games and settings searches.
- Configurable controller button combinations and quick-menu favorites, with separate global and per-game preferences.
- Disc-change prompts can suggest a matching disc from the current folder for quick loading, while retaining manual browsing.
- Optional Samsung performance controls and per-game support for compatible graphics layers, including ExynosTools/MdiEx packages.

## Interface, controls and everyday use

- Updated app branding and startup presentation, with a new boot video, splash transition and app icon.
- Refreshed adaptive layouts for different mobile aspect ratios, display cutouts and large screens.
- Menus and editors stay within the content area, keeping navigation and the contextual hintbar available.
- Refreshed achievement notification styling.
- Cover-sized game cards, compact on-cover controls and favorites indicators, clearer home/library organization, and contextual controller hints.
- Artwork display modes for disc art, cover art or cover art with fallback; clearer refresh controls and snoozable provider-limit notices.
- Improved navigation preserves searches, selections and scroll positions when returning from settings and nested pages.
- Expanded performance overlay with optional CPU/RAM information, available device GPU metrics and selectable temperature sources. Temperature values now use a compact display without sensor-name annotations.
- Broader English, Italian, German, French, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese coverage across Android screens, native menus and setting descriptions.
- Refined experimental phone vibration with gentler effects and separate intensity controls.
- Expanded integration with ES-DE, Daijishō, Beacon, Retro Hrai and Cocoon Shell.
- Guided import of supported library and touch-layout data from the previous app.
- Clearer content/driver cleanup confirmations and safer handling of unrelated games, saves and settings.

## Compatibility reports and community features

- Rebuilt opt-in compatibility reporting with four playability ratings, reviewable local drafts, recovery of interrupted sessions and scheduled uploads.
- Reports are organized by game, with batch deletion and manual per-game reporting exclusions.
- Reports retain configuration details and separate results when settings change during a session. Uploads are deferred while a game is running.
- Compatibility pages on the website retain individual session reports and existing community data, with hardware, driver and app-version filters and expandable configuration details.
- Report authors can add descriptive notes and clarify driver names while preserving the original measurements. Administration includes correction history and batch moderation tools.

## Core, game fixes and performance

- General compatibility and performance work across graphics, shaders, runtime timing, storage, audio and input in the updated core.
- Startup and loading improvements affecting Naruto: Rise of a Ninja, Metro 2033, Wolfenstein: The New Order and Peter Jackson's King Kong.
- Stability, rendering and performance improvements for Need for Speed: The Run, with optional visual adjustments.
- Performance and timing work checked in Ninety-Nine Nights and Naruto: Rise of a Ninja, with stutter improvements in tested Assassin's Creed scenes.
- Rendering improvements for BioShock 2, and rendering/runtime stability improvements for Fable II.
- Rendering improvements for Viva Piñata, plus an optional experimental stability patch.
- Audio fixes checked in Blood Drive and Grand Theft Auto V, with clearer required-update guidance for GTA V.
- Partial rendering improvements and compatibility profiles for Splinter Cell Conviction, Blue Dragon, Rise of the Tomb Raider and Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions. Splinter Cell Conviction also received performance work in tested scenes.
- Improved startup, pause/resume, session shutdown and shader-cache reliability.
- Reduced unnecessary background and overlay work, with a dedicated Power and thermal settings section and optional efficiency controls.

## Important notes

- TV mode and synchronized player profiles are still highly experimental and may have bugs or reliability issues.
- Some game improvements require the appropriate compatibility settings or supported graphics features. Results vary by game, scene, device and driver.
- Assassin's Creed still has an unresolved GPU crash. Blue Dragon, Wolfenstein: The New Order and Rise of the Tomb Raider retain known visual issues; Splinter Cell Conviction improvements remain partial.
- Frame interpolation smooths displayed motion; guest simulation speed is unchanged. GPU cost and input latency depend on the chosen settings.
- Live Lobbies supports System Link games rather than Xbox Live services. Direct Internet connections depend on network conditions; relay fallback is not included.
- Sensor readings, Samsung controls and graphics-layer compatibility depend on the device and package version. Some original texture-layer packages still have known compatibility issues. Custom graphics packages are not bundled with the app.
- Achievement synchronization does not provide cloud save synchronization. Compatibility reporting remains optional.

releases.name: ARMSX2 nightly 20261114 (6d9511e29e)
releases.body:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- macOS: a refused notarization is not a build failure
- arm64: the crash post-mortem's microVU readers are Linux only
- GameDB: Stuntman and Driv3r run the EE at Exact clamping
- arm64: a SIGILL gets the crash post-mortem too
- arm64: the crash post-mortem names where the lr points
- arm64: the crash post-mortem's VU microcode comes from the program's copy
- arm64: the crash post-mortem names the library a pc outside the JIT is in
- arm64: the crash post-mortem shows the VU microcode at the fault block
- arm64: the crash post-mortem names the microVU block that holds the pc
- LSFG: rebuild the swap chain before the acquire, and make it FIFO
- microVU: don't finish VU1 through a dispatcher that does not exist
- Tests: a second boot after a VM that stopped with VU1 busy

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261113...6d9511e29e3e00d5ab78899f5292b967ab850ddb

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.3
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.3 So, our bug reporting feature was a wild success. Thank you to all the users who submitted reports. Many of them are great reports and will be useful for fixing issues, however many of them were not. The app now explains that you can’t run PS2 games on a PS1 BIOS. Also, you can’t run Turnip drivers on Mali GPUs, and a dozen of other common user errors. We also tell you if you left your refrigerator door open ;) Anyways, here's what's new: VR mode is here: play side by side in a phone headset, with the picture's size, distance and height set to fit your lenses. DNS host entries get names and on/off switches, touch sticks get an adjustable travel, and the driver list shows only the drivers built for your GPU, now with MdiEx as a drives source for Exynos devices. When a game can't start, ARMSX2 tells you why and what to do, and problem reports carry the log of the run before. Shadow of the Colossus, Stuntman and Spider-Man 3 draw their shadows faster, the ARM64 graphics, video and sound code is quicker, and the emulator needs less memory. ## New **VR mode (side by side).** For phone headsets: the game is drawn once in each half of the screen. VR picture size, VR picture distance and VR picture height fit the two pictures to your headset and lenses. Upscaling, TV shaders and frame generation still apply, and the on-screen controls step aside while VR mode is on, so play with a controller. Find it in Settings > Renderer and in the pause menu's Graphics tab. done by @jpolo1224 **Named DNS host entries.** In Settings > Network, each DNS host entry has a name, its hostname and IP address, an Enabled switch and Remove this host, so entries for several games can stay in the list and be switched on when needed. The screen reminds you that the entries are used only when Primary DNS or Secondary DNS is set to Internal. done by @jpolo1224 **Stick travel.** Settings > Controls > On-Screen Controls has a Stick travel slider, from 50 to 250%, that sets how far your thumb moves for full tilt on every touch stick. Lower reaches full tilt sooner, higher gives finer control, and the thumb art reaches the ring's edge at full tilt either way. done by @jpolo1224 **Drivers for your GPU.** The GPU Driver list shows only the drivers built for your device's GPU: the Turnip and Adreno Tools packs on Adreno, MaliSX2 on the Mali GPUs it supports, and the Exynos packs on Xclipse, where avavo's MdiEx releases now join the list. A release with one file per chip lists each one by name, like MdiEx 1480 v3.6, and on supported Mali GPUs the driver card recommends MaliSX2. Importing a driver zip works on every device. done by @bmdhacks and @jpolo1224 (This picture shows off the new driver source, and was taken before the change to only show GPU drivers pertaining to your device, Adreno/Mali/Exynos drivers etc). **Clear answers when a game can't start.** If the BIOS is missing, can't be read, isn't a PS2 BIOS, or is a PS1 BIOS like the ps1_rom.bin copied from a PS3, the message says so and points you to BIOS Location to import your PS2's BIOS. When the graphics driver can't start the renderer, a popup message gives the reason, such as ANGLE on an older driver that offers only OpenGL ES 2.0. done by @bmdhacks **Problem reports say more.** Reports also send the log of the run before, cleaned the same way as the current one, so a game that froze and was closed still gets its log to the developers. When a game stops on an emulation error or crashes, the log holds a detailed account of what the emulated CPU and the recompilers were doing at that moment. done by @bmdhacks **Automatic Performance Tuning tries more.** For a game held back by the GPU, it first lowers Display Resolution (HW scaler) to the size the game renders at, which keeps every rendered detail. Hardware Download Mode now steps through Async, No Readbacks and Disabled, and a step that didn't help no longer stops it from trying the next. Changing Display Resolution yourself in a game's settings turns tuning off for that game, like the other tuned settings. done by @bmdhacks **Every new setting in every language.** VR mode, the DNS host entries, Stick travel and the new BIOS messages are in all 19 of the app's languages. done by @jpolo1224 ## Faster **Shadows in Shadow of the Colossus, Spider-Man 3 and Stuntman.** In Vulkan, the passes these games use to count shadow volumes are counted in the stencil buffer instead of being blended into a high-precision copy of the screen. On the RG 55G1, Shadow of the Colossus spends about a third less GPU time per frame; on a Retroid Pocket Flip 2 at 2x, Stuntman runs about 14% faster and Spider-Man 3 about 5% faster. done by @bmdhacks **Fewer clears in Jak 3 and similar games.** When a draw reads the image it is drawing to, Vulkan skips clearing the copy it reads from whenever the draw can't sample outside that copy. In Jak 3 that is up to about 274 clears a frame. done by @bmdhacks **IOP thread on the slower cores.** With the IOP thread on, it runs on the slower cores, leaving the fast ones to the EE, GS and VU1 threads. On chips with four fast cores, like the Dimensity 7300, that leaves a fast core for the app's own drawing, such as the on-screen controls. done by @bmdhacks **Gran Turismo 4.** The game database turns the IOP thread on for Gran Turismo 4, which takes the sound mixing off the EE thread. done by @sunshineinabox **Graphics code on ARM64.** Palette and colour table conversions, GIF packet checks, texture hashing, GS readbacks and the vertex kick all do less work, and a palette lookup or draw pipeline that repeats is reused instead of looked up again. done by @sunshineinabox **Bigger GIF buffers.** On devices with 2 GB of RAM or more, the GIF's path 2 and 3 buffers hold 32 MB, so large image uploads keep the EE running instead of waiting on the GS. done by @sunshineinabox **Videos, texture packs and sound.** FMVs decode with a NEON inverse DCT, texture packs decode BC7 and JPEG images with NEON, and audio time stretching uses NEON dot products. done by @sunshineinabox **Vulkan with VSync off.** Vulkan keeps three swapchain images when VSync is off, so getting the next image doesn't wait on the compositor. done by @sunshineinabox **Touch sticks.** Moving a touch stick only moves its thumb on screen, without rebuilding the controls for every finger movement. On-screen controls can also now be toggled from the quick menu. done by @bmdhacks **Less memory.** ARMSX2 clears the emulated memory at boot without taking hundreds of megabytes of RAM for it, the recompilers' block tables use memory only for the parts a game touches, and microVU's jump tables take memory as they fill: about 58 MB less in a God of War II scene. done by @sunshineinabox and @bmdhacks **Optimized build trained on this release.** The profile behind the optimized build is retrained on this release's code across the same 16 games. done by @bmdhacks ## Fixed **Auto Progressive Scan in Burnout 3.** Burnout 3: Takedown and other Criterion games ask for the progressive scan combo late in their intro, after the publisher logos, so Auto Progressive Scan now holds it until 30 seconds into the game. done by @jpolo1224 **Lines on Mali Bifrost GPUs.** With Vulkan on Bifrost GPUs like the Mali-G52 and Mali-G76, MaliSX2 included, the line shader reads only vertices inside the draw, so games that draw lines keep running. Found while reviewing a pull request by @Matheus290 (#954). done by @bmdhacks **Mali shader compiles.** Vulkan's conversion, present and FXAA shaders get texture sizes from the app instead of asking the GPU, so they compile on the Mali drivers that couldn't compile that query, and anisotropic filtering does the same on Mali drivers older than r30. done by @sunshineinabox **MaliSX2 and PanVK.** A workaround meant for Arm's own Mali driver now applies only there, so MaliSX2 and PanVK keep every stencil clear, and PanVK keeps push descriptors. done by @sunshineinabox **ANGLE after the device's OpenGL ES driver.** Starting a game on ANGLE after one on the device's own OpenGL ES driver, without restarting the app, works reliably. done by @bmdhacks **Resume after an emulation error.** Pressing Resume after a game stops on an emulation error shows the error again and keeps the game paused, instead of closing the app. done by @bmdhacks **VSync after switching renderers.** After switching from Vulkan to OpenGL and back in a game, Vulkan keeps the VSync mode you chose. Based on a pull request by @Matheus290 (#955). done by @bmdhacks **RetroAchievements.** Android uses the same RetroAchievements runtime as Linux and iOS, rcheevos 12.5, with its fixes for achievement sets that use {recall} and for malformed data (#941). done by @Matheus290 ## More accurate **Emulator core on ARM64.** The VU1 thread's ring buffer never overwrites work that hasn't been read yet, IPU colour conversion with alpha thresholds covers the whole block, the optional NEON reverb clamps at every step like the default path, and R8G8B8 DDS replacement textures read only their own data. Floating-point trap settings and the recompilers' jump buffers are set correctly, and generated code stays clear of Cortex-A53 erratum 843419. done by @sunshineinabox **Software renderer texture coordinates.** Textures drawn with extreme S, T and Q values land where a real PS2 puts them, following measurements of 8,245 cases on an SCPH-30001 console: the sign of Q carries over to S and T, and coordinates stop at the console's limits. done by @bmdhacks ## Linux **Big Picture.** Choice dialogs open on the option already chosen (#959), and the keyboard and gamepad cursor stays visible after the on-screen keyboard closes (#958). Based on pull requests by @Matheus290. done by @bmdhacks **Game list at startup in the SDL build.** The SDL build scans your game folders when it starts, and picking a game during the scan no longer waits for it to finish (#947). Based on a pull request by @Matheus290. done by @bmdhacks **This Game texture packs.** The texture pack browser, in the Qt build and in Big Picture, gets a This Game list while a game runs, with only that game's packs. done by @bmdhacks **Missing CPU features named.** On an ARM64 CPU without a feature the build needs, ARMSX2 says which one when it starts. done by @sunshineinabox **Mali under Wayland.** Vulkan recreates a window surface that reports no formats, as Arm's driver can under Wayland. done by @sunshineinabox All the speed, memory and accuracy work above is in the Linux builds as well.

releases.name: Bannerhub v3.8.1
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Only install official stable releases** (like this one). Do NOT install pre-releases or raw CI artifacts — pre-release builds use a different package name (`com.tencent.ig`) and cannot be upgraded to stable without uninstalling first.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Microphone permission required for Voice Chat.** When you activate voice chat (dashboard → Game Configs → Voice Chat), BannerHub will prompt for the **Microphone** permission. You must allow it for in-game calls to work — without it the call falls back to opening in your browser.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Notification permission required.** BannerHub will prompt for the **Post Notifications** permission when you start your first Epic, GOG, or Amazon download. You must allow it to receive download progress and completion notifications.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Files access required for SD card storage.** To save games to your SD card, BannerHub must be granted the **Files and Media** permission (Android Settings → Apps → BannerHub → Permissions → Files and media → Allow management of all files). Without it the SD card toggle has no effect.

## 🛠️ Games work on the new GameHub firmware (1.4.8 / 1.4.9)

With the **GameHub** API source, a fresh install downloads GameHub's newest firmware (1.4.8 or 1.4.9). That firmware **removes `libGameScopeVK.so`**. BannerHub points games at that graphics library, and the AI Frame Generation engine lives in it. On v3.8.0 **every game closed a few seconds after launching** (OpenGL titles crashed outright), and AI Frame Generation was gone.

- **Automatic restore.** BannerHub now carries its own copy of the library (the one shipped in firmware 1.3.7 – 1.4.2) and puts it back before each game launch whenever it's missing. Games start again and **AI Frame Generation keeps working**, with the same engine as before.
- **Future-proof.** If a later firmware removes or renames the library again, BannerHub restores it the same way. A library the firmware provides itself is never replaced.
- **Nothing to do.** No reinstall and no settings change: update, then launch a game.

**Validation:** fresh install on firmware 1.4.9 with the GameHub API source. BannerHub restored the library on the first launch, games ran, and AI Frame Generation worked.

## 💾 SD card toggle works without a GHL folder

**Save Store Games to External Storage (SD Card)** used to say *"No SD card found"* unless the card already had a `GHL` folder at its root (an old GameHub convention). BannerHub now accepts any writable SD card and creates the `bannerhub/` folder itself. That's the folder GOG, Epic and Amazon games install into (`{SD card}/bannerhub/{store}/{game}/`). Internal storage is never mistaken for the SD card, and Steam storage is unaffected.

## 🧩 Component Manager: removed components stay removed

Removing a component (single remove or **Remove All**) now also clears it from GameHub's saved component registry, so it no longer comes back after the app restarts.

## Credits

- **SD card detection fix:** **[tirsomb](https://github.com/tirsomb)** via [PR #108 "fix: detect writable SD card without GHL marker"](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/pull/108), found and tested on an LG V60.
- AI Frame Generation engine by the **GameHub team**. All v3.8.0 features (in-game voice chat, per-game PC Audio Settings) remain active.

### Tracking BannerHub updates

- **This repo's [Releases page](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases)** — watch the repo to get notified.
- **[Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium)** — add `https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub` as an app source with **"Reconcile version string with version detected from OS"** enabled.

### Upgrading

- **v3.8.0 → v3.8.1:** install the matching variant directly over your existing install. No certificate change, no data loss.
- **v3.7.0 or earlier → v3.8.1:** install normally. If the signing certificate differs, uninstall first.

---

For the in-game voice chat and per-game PC Audio Settings added in v3.8.0, see the [v3.8.0 release notes](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.8.0).

You must allow it for in-game calls to work — without it the call falls back to opening in your browser. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Notification permission required.** BannerHub will prompt for the **Post Notifications** permission when you start your first Epic, GOG, or Amazon download.
