Without it the SD card toggle has no effect. ## 🎙️ In-game voice chat (no Steam, no root) BannerHub now has a **built-in voice chat** you can use while in a game — **no Steam account, no root, no extra app**. Identity is just a **nickname** you pick plus a stable per-install id; there are no friends lists and no ringing. It's a **room model**: Create or Join a room by a short code, or share a join link. - **Two-gate activation.** A new **Voice Chat** item appears in the dashboard side menu under **Game Configs** → nickname field + **Check availability**. An **Activate** toggle stays disabled until the name is confirmed free; ticking it claims the name and turns the in-game pill on. - **In-game pill + room box.** A draggable edge pill opens a room box with the live **roster** (everyone's nickname), a call **timer**, and **Mute** / **Leave**. The pill stays pinned to the edge while the box drags freely, with a collapsible **opacity** slider. - **Cross-play with BannerHub v6.** Voice rides the **same WebRTC mesh** (BannerHub Cloudflare Worker + Cloudflare Realtime TURN) that BannerHub v6 uses, so a **BannerHub user and a BannerHub v6 user can share the same room and talk**, in either direction. Room codes use the same format on both builds. **Device-confirmed both ways across different networks.** ## 🔊 Per-game PC Audio Settings (recording-compatible mode) A new **PC Audio Settings** entry in each game's popup options menu (right after **PC Vibration Settings**) fixes **silent screen recordings**. Stock GameHub loads `module-aaudio-sink` with no performance-mode argument, so PulseAudio opens a `LOW_LATENCY` AAudio stream the framework grants as exclusive MMAP — which **bypasses the mixer that screen recorders tap**. The result: recordings capture video but **no game audio** whenever the in-game audio driver is PulseAudio (ALSA records fine). - **PulseAudio mode: Low latency (default) / Recording-compatible.** Recording-compatible appends `pm=0` to the sink line → `PERFORMANCE_MODE_NONE` → the stream stays on the mixer so screen recordings capture in-game sound. - The active game's `gameId` is resolved from the live `WineActivity`'s `WineActivityData` field (the 5.3.5 launch intent carries no `gameId` extra), and the setting lives in `pc_g_setting`, so **Export / Import Config** carries it automatically. ### Tracking BannerHub updates - **This repo's [Releases page](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases)** — watch the repo to get notified. - **[Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium)** — add `https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub` as an app source with **"Reconcile version string with version detected from OS"** enabled. ### Upgrading - **v3.7.5 → v3.8.0:** install the matching variant directly over your existing install. No certificate change, no data loss. - **v3.7.0 or earlier → v3.8.0:** install normally. If the signing certificate differs, uninstall first.

releases.name: Bannerhub v3.7.5
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Only install official stable releases** (like this one). Do NOT install pre-releases or raw CI artifacts — pre-release builds use a different package name (`com.tencent.ig`) and cannot be upgraded to stable without uninstalling first.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Notification permission required.** BannerHub will prompt for the **Post Notifications** permission when you start your first Epic, GOG, or Amazon download. You must allow it to receive download progress and completion notifications. Without it, you will not be notified when downloads finish or fail.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Files access required for SD card storage.** To save games to your SD card, BannerHub must be granted the **Files and Media** permission. Go to **Android Settings → Apps → BannerHub → Permissions → Files and media** and set it to **Allow management of all files** (or equivalent on your device). Without this permission the SD card toggle will have no effect.

## Offline launch for imported PC games

**Imported PC games (and any non-Steam game source) now launch offline.**

Pre-3.7.5, putting the device in airplane mode or on a network without internet and tapping an imported PC game would abort the launch with `Game configuration file download failed`. Steam library games had a partial offline bypass already; the other four game source types (imported via the PC Game Manager, local-file import, server-downloaded, and unknown) did not.

v3.7.5 adds a no-network skip on the three setup tasks that previously required a network call: `GameConfigDownloadTask` (fetches per-game env config from the server), `SetGameRecommConfigTask` (applies server-pushed recommendations), and `DependencyInstallTask` (checks the server for new dep versions). When `NetworkUtils.r()` reports no network, those tasks are skipped and the launch proceeds with whatever components, container, and Wine version were set up the last time the game launched online.

In practice:

- **Any game that has launched online at least once will now launch offline.** Wine boots, the game runs, the previously-applied container settings persist.
- **Steam library games unaffected.** Their existing offline support is unchanged.
- **Self-healing on reconnect.** When you come back online, the next launch hits the full pipeline and re-syncs any server-pushed recommendations or dep updates. The offline window doesn't accumulate drift.
- **No behavior change online.** All three patches are pure additions wrapped in `if no network: skip; else: original code`. The online path runs the original 3.7.4 logic byte-for-byte. Verified by code review and pre1→pre4 device iteration.

### Known limitations

1. **First-ever launches still require network** — if a game has never been set up at all, no components/container are on disk to fall back to. This release only fixes the second-and-later offline launches.
2. **Stale per-game settings** — if you change a per-game setting (Box64 variant, container, etc.) and then go offline before the next launch, the offline launch uses the previous on-disk setup. Workaround: relaunch once online after changing settings, then go offline.
3. **Server-pushed component recommendations skipped offline** — practical impact nil for games already working; deferred to the next online launch.

### Tracking BannerHub updates

- **This GitHub repo's [Releases page](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases)** — watch the repo to get notified
- **[Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium)** — add `https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub` as an app source with **"Reconcile version string with version detected from OS"** enabled

### Upgrading

- v3.7.4 → v3.7.5: install the matching variant directly over your existing install. No certificate change, no data loss.
- v3.7.0 or earlier → v3.7.5: install normally. If the signing certificate differs, uninstall first.

releases.name: Bannerhub v3.7.4
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Only install official stable releases** (like this one). Do NOT install pre-releases or raw CI artifacts — pre-release builds use a different package name (`com.tencent.ig`) and cannot be upgraded to stable without uninstalling first.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Notification permission required.** BannerHub will prompt for the **Post Notifications** permission when you start your first Epic, GOG, or Amazon download. You must allow it to receive download progress and completion notifications.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Files access required for SD card storage.** To save games to your SD card, BannerHub must be granted the **Files and Media** permission (**Android Settings → Apps → BannerHub → Permissions → Files and media → Allow management of all files**). Without it the SD card toggle has no effect.

## What's new in v3.7.4

One focused fix: **PC Vibration / Rumble no longer breaks x86_64 / Box64 game launches.**

### The problem (v3.7.0 – v3.7.3)

The PC Vibration / Rumble feature added in v3.7.0 loaded a small helper library, `libevshim.so`, into the Wine process via `LD_PRELOAD` to keep sustained rumble alive (SDL2 otherwise auto-stops the motor after ~1 second). That worked on arm64 / FEX containers — but on **Box64**, mapping that extra library into the game's address space corrupted the dynarec and made **every x86_64 game launch die at startup** with `c000007b` / `wine has died`. If you ran x86_64 titles under Box64 on v3.7.0–v3.7.3, this is the regression that was killing your games.

### The fix (v3.7.4) — preload-free

v3.7.4 removes `libevshim.so` entirely. **No extra library is mapped into Wine anymore**, so the crash class is eliminated. Sustained rumble is preserved by patching every `winebus.so` in the container **on disk** so SDL2's ~1 s rumble auto-expiry never fires:

- **aarch64-unix** and **x86_64-unix (Box64)** byte patterns are both handled, with the rumble-*stop* call sites left untouched so release-on-let-go still works.
- Safety net: if the x86_64 pattern ever misses on a future Proton, the unmatched `winebus.so` is dumped to the app's external files directory for re-derivation rather than failing silently.
- Everything else about the feature is unchanged — independent low/high motors, single-motor blend, instant release, multi-controller auto-wake, the per-game **PC Vibration Settings** dialog, and Export/Import config. Same continuous-rumble behavior, no library injected, no launch regression.

### Validation

Device-verified before promotion:

- **Launch regression cleared:** Dead Cells and ULTRAKILL launch cleanly on **Box64 "Extreme"**, DOOMBLADE on **FEX** — no `c000007b`, no crash, no dump.
- **Dirt 3** (x86_64 / Box64): a clean **~26-minute** session with **sustained continuous rumble** confirmed in-game (no more ~1 s SDL cutoff). Wine log showed zero `evshim` tags (library fully removed, as expected) and no x86_64 dump fallback — the on-disk pattern matched this Proton build.
- **Manual in-container check:** rumble was also tested directly by running **`GameConTest.exe`** (Microsoft's XInput GameController Tester) manually inside the container, driving the low and high motors on demand to confirm the on-disk `winebus.so` patch holds the motor through sustained input independent of any specific game.

## Upgrading

- **v3.7.x → v3.7.4:** install the matching variant directly over your existing install. No certificate change, no data loss. All vibration settings (`bh_vibration_*` in `pc_g_setting<gameId>`) carry over untouched.
- **Earlier → v3.7.4:** install normally. If the signing certificate differs, uninstall first.
- Variants with different package names cannot replace each other in-place.

## Credits

- **PC-accurate Vibration / Rumble** — original feature by **[TideGear](https://github.com/TideGear)** via [PR #80](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/pull/80), rebased from [GameNative PR #1214](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1214) by the same author.
- **v3.7.4 x86_64 / Box64 preload-free rework** — also by **[TideGear](https://github.com/TideGear)**, contributed as [PR #91 "Make Vibration Fix Compatible With x86_64 Containers"](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/pull/91). The PR was closed on 2026-05-16 after its code was adopted directly into BannerHub with TideGear's explicit permission.
- AI Frame Generation engine by the **GameHub team**; the v3.7.3 GOG reliability overhaul ported from [`utkarshdalal/GameNative`](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative). All v3.7.x features remain active.

**Please go support GameNative: https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative**

## Community Game Configs

The in-app Community Game Configs browser currently serves **1,321 games** with **4,840 device-specific configs** contributed by the community.

## Installation

See https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub#installation for CPU/variant selection and step-by-step setup.

---

For the v3.7.0 baseline (AI Frame Generation menu, PC Vibration / Rumble) see the [v3.7.0 release notes](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.7.0); for the GOG multi-CDN overhaul + FrameGen onResume fix see [v3.7.3](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.7.3).

releases.name: Bannerhub v3.7.3
releases.body: > [!WARNING] > **Only install official stable releases** (like this one). Do NOT install pre-releases or raw CI artifacts — pre-release builds use a different package name (`com.tencent.ig`) and cannot be upgraded to stable without uninstalling first. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Notification permission required.** BannerHub will prompt for the **Post Notifications** permission when you start your first Epic, GOG, or Amazon download. You must allow it to receive download progress and completion notifications. Without it, you will not be notified when downloads finish or fail. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Files access required for SD card storage.** To save games to your SD card, BannerHub must be granted the **Files and Media** permission. Go to **Android Settings → Apps → BannerHub → Permissions → Files and media** and set it to **Allow management of all files** (or equivalent on your device). Without this permission the SD card toggle will have no effect. ## What's new in v3.7.3 Two independent reliability fixes, both device-confirmed. ### 1. GOG downloads — multi-CDN failover + resumable PARTIAL state GOG ships every depot through several CDN endpoints — typically `cdn.gog.com`, `gog-cdn-fastly.gog.com`, `gog-cdn-akamai.gog.com`, and a couple of region-specific mirrors. Up until v3.7.2 BannerHub picked one and abandoned the whole download if that CDN returned 403 / 404 / 5xx on a single file. v3.7.3 fixes this top-to-bottom. - **Automatic failover.** Each file probes every CDN advertised in the depot manifest in order; the first one that succeeds wins. A single bad endpoint no longer kills the install. - **CDN picker on the install dialog.** A new "CDN" row sits alongside size and storage on the install-confirm dialog. Leave it on **Auto** (default) for round-robin failover, or pin a specific CDN if your network plays better with one — useful when an ISP throttles a particular hostname or when GOG's own routing sends you to a degraded edge. - **↻ Refresh button.** Tap the refresh icon on the picker to re-fetch the live CDN list from GOG without dismissing the dialog. Use this if you opened the dialog, walked away for a while, and CDNs have rotated. - **PARTIAL install state.** When a download is interrupted (cancel, kill, OOM, network drop), BannerHub now records `gog_state_=PARTIAL` with the in-flight file index + byte offset. Re-tapping install picks up from the same point instead of starting over. All three GOG UIs (library list, library grid, game-detail dialog) now share one install-state model — the checkmark / Add Game / Resume affordances are consistent everywhere. - **Diagnostic toast.** When a file does fail across every CDN, the error toast now names the file, the last CDN tried, and the HTTP code. The same line is also appended to `bh_gog_debug.txt` (in your app's external files directory) so you can copy-paste an exact failure into a bug report. **Device-confirmed during pre-release testing:** POSTAL 2 (multi-CDN fallback survived a single-CDN failure mid-install), Citadel Remonstered (468/468 files clean on Auto), CDN picker UI, ↻ Refresh button. ### 2. AI Frame Generation — resume reliability + cleaner gear dialog Three issues from v3.7.0 / v3.7.1 / v3.7.2 are addressed in one bundle. - **Frame-gen no longer "lies" after resume.** Previously, the `gamescope.control` bytes were only written on first launch. Pressing Home or locking the screen and resuming the game left the sidebar switch saying **ON** while the AI overlay was silently dead — your FPS would drop back to native without the switch ever changing state. The launch hook now also runs on `WineActivity.onResume`, so the overlay survives every backgrounding cycle. If the sidebar switch says ON, AI frame generation is **actually on**. - **Gear icon hides when the switch is OFF.** The gear button next to the sidebar switch now defaults to hidden and only appears when AI Frame Generation is enabled. Matches the existing pattern used by RTS controls in the same sidebar. - **Dialog cleanup — game view stays visible.** The settings dialog no longer paints a full-screen black background over your game. It now uses Android's translucent dim with the game rendering live underneath at 60% dim, the same way native system dialogs look. The dialog has three controls — Preset slider, Custom flow scale slider, and a blue **Close** button — and tap-outside also dismisses. The multiplier picker is gone (it was always 2× on tested hardware anyway; the value is now hardcoded) and the redundant in-dialog Enable switch is gone (the sidebar switch is the single source of truth). Net result: faster to operate, easier on the eyes, no behavior loss. ## Upgrading - **v3.7.2 → v3.7.3:** install the matching variant directly over your existing install. No certificate change, no data loss. GOG library + install state are preserved (`bh_gog_prefs` keys are forward-compatible — old completed installs read as `INSTALLED`, no migration needed). FrameGen settings (`bh_framegen.xml`) carry over; the removed `multiplier` key is simply ignored. - **v3.7.1 or earlier → v3.7.3:** install normally. If the signing certificate differs, uninstall first. - Variants with different package names cannot replace each other in-place. ## Credits - **GOG download reliability overhaul** ported from upstream [`utkarshdalal/GameNative`](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative): multi-CDN [PR #1220](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1220) + [PR #1219](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1219) by **Utkarsh Dalal** (with co-author **Jeremy Bernstein** on #1219), CDN picker [PR #1215](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1215) by **Bart Zaalberg**, install-state PARTIAL [PR #1277](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1277) by **Joshua Tam**. - **AI Frame Generation onResume + dialog cleanup** ported from [Bannerhub-Lite PR #5](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerhub-Lite/pull/5) by **[teldommm](https://github.com/teldommm)**. - All v3.7.0 features (AI Frame Generation engine itself by the **GameHub team**, PC-accurate Vibration / Rumble by [TideGear](https://github.com/TideGear) via [GameNative PR #1214](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative/pull/1214)) remain active. **Please go support GameNative: https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative** --- For details on the v3.7.0 baseline (AI Frame Generation menu, PC Vibration / Rumble), see the [v3.7.0 release notes](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.7.0). For the v3.7.1 / v3.7.2 upgrade-prompt stubs, see the [v3.7.1](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.7.1) and [v3.7.2](https://github.com/The412Banner/BannerHub/releases/tag/v3.7.2) release notes.

releases.name: Minimum System Requirements for Winlator WB64
releases.body:
[![logo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed1525e8-b05f-4e93-8003-933146b27dd9)](https://github.com/winebox64/winlator/releases)



# Minimum System Requirements for Winlator WB64:
- __OS (Operating System):__ Android 7.0 or later
- __Processor/CPU (Central Processing Unit):__ Qualcomm Snapdragon 460 or higher
- __GPU (Graphics Processing Unit):__ Adreno 610 or higher 
- __Graphics API:__ Vulkan 1.1 or higher
- __Internal Storage:__ At least 2GB of free space
- __RAM (Random Access Memory):__ At least 1GB of free RAM available, depending on the game requirments
- __Root Access:__ Not required
- __Gamepad:__ Optional (xinput/xbox recommended)


__NOTE: Recommended for game titles released before 2013 or DX9-based, Some games especially those from 2013 onwards, may experience performance issues.__
__Results can vary based on the device used, environmental conditions, and other factors, such as simultaneous processing, and different processor capabilities.__

__Please be careful when downloading from other websites. We recommend downloading only from this GitHub repository or official.__

✅ __[WINLATOR.ORG](https://winlator.org) is the original site.__ 

⚠️ __while [~WINLATOR.COM~](https://github.com/winebox64/winlator/releases), [~WINLATOR.APP~](https://github.com/winebox64/winlator/releases) and others are fake.__
__Never share your E-mail address or any other personal information.__ ⚠️

----

### Why does glibc run slower than Proot on some Android devices?
**1. glibc vs. Android’s bionic libc**
Android uses bionic libc, which is lightweight and optimized for mobile devices.
Running glibc on Android often requires additional compatibility layers, like proot + glibc rootfs, which might introduce performance overhead.
**2. Syscall Translation Overhead**
Proot uses syscall translation, which can be slow in general.
However, on Android, some glibc syscalls may not be well-optimized or may rely on emulation layers, making native glibc performance worse.
**3. Filesystem Overhead**
Proot uses overlay filesystems, which can sometimes optimize game data access.
A direct glibc setup might suffer from filesystem incompatibilities on Android.
**4. Memory & CPU Constraints**
Android optimizes bionic for low-memory usage.
Running glibc-based games might trigger higher RAM usage, leading to CPU throttling or inefficient memory access.
**5. Native vs. Emulated Execution**
Proot can sometimes optimize syscall handling by redirecting them efficiently.
glibc-based games might not be fully optimized for Android’s kernel, leading to bottlenecks.

releases.name: hakuX 1.3.0
releases.body:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise
- **Morrowind** — no longer freezes when you leave a building: disc and hard-disk reads now take a little time, as on the console. The inventory's character is drawn properly: it no longer stands on red with a black band over its head, or leaves ghost copies of itself around it when you change gear after a load
- **Halo 2** — the fog no longer shows as stripes that move with the camera, and with the scope up the view around it is dimmed with black lines, not light blue
- **Munch's Oddysee** — no dark box over the ground under the characters' shadows
- **Project Zero II (PAL)** — no longer hangs on its first frame
- **Amped 2** — no longer crashes as its first level loads
- **Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks** — the models no longer explode on Mali-G57 GPUs
- **Burnout 2: Point of Impact** — no longer crashes as it starts
- **Def Jam: Fight for NY** — no longer freezes on one frame at the intro cutscene: while hakuX holds a game up (such as while its shaders compile), the game's clock now waits too
- **Double-S.T.E.A.L: The Second Clash** — no longer stops as its first scene begins, and the screen is no longer black, also after loading a savestate
- **Soldier of Fortune II: Double Helix** — no longer crashes when you skip an intro movie
- **Touge R** — races are no longer black under the HUD

### Performance
- **Network** — with the network on (system link or XLink Kai), the console no longer keeps most of a CPU core busy

### App
- **On-screen controls editor** — its toolbar wraps onto more rows on narrower screens, such as 4:3 handhelds, instead of pushing buttons off the edge

releases.name: hakuX 1.2.0
releases.body:
System link, stability and compatibility improvements.

### Network
- **System link over your network** — Settings → Network → System link → LAN: hakuX devices on the same Wi-Fi network find each other as Xbox consoles on a LAN do. Devices the network's broadcasts don't reach, on another subnet or a VPN such as ZeroTier or Tailscale, are added by address under Other consoles
- **XLink Kai** — system link over the Internet through an XLink Kai engine running on a computer on your network; its web page picks the game's arena
- **Console identity** — each console has its own serial number, network address and online key. A device whose hard disk was copied from another one offers to make itself a new identity, since two consoles with one identity can't see each other


### Games
- **Sega GT 2002** — the cars have their paint, reflections and sun highlights
- **Doom 3** — no longer crashes as its main menu loads
- **Fatal Frame II** — starts and reads its disc in the order it asks for
- **AirForce Delta Storm** — answers the controller and the on-screen controls (it ignored all input)
- **Silent Hill 2** — no longer crashes when it loads a room
- **Splinter Cell: Double Agent** — no longer closes on boot
- **Super Monkey Ball Deluxe** — its title movie plays and its movies aren't black
- **Ultimate Spider-Man** — no longer crashes a second into boot
- **Grand Theft Auto III** — no longer shows its bad-disc screen
- **Project Gotham Racing 2** — the attract replay no longer goes black
- **Dungeons & Dragons Heroes** — the tutorial's prompts show
- **Sound** — games that hold their voices while the sound engine updates them, or stop a voice as it changes, no longer freeze or play a stopped voice on

### Performance
- **Fewer stutters with Turnip** — frames reach the screen without a CPU wait in front of each one

### App
- **Controllers** — only the players with a controller are plugged into the console (player 1 always, for the on-screen controls), and a controller plugs in or out as it connects, disconnects or is assigned to another player, without restarting the game

releases.name: hakuX 1.1.0
releases.body:
GPUs beyond Adreno (experimental).

### GPUs
- **Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR (experimental)** — hakuX runs on GPUs other than Adreno: features they lack are replaced (BC and 4444 textures decoded up front, standard border colours, the push block in a buffer, D32S8 depth), and known driver bugs are worked around (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`). Burnout 3 and Mercenaries run cleanly on a Pixel 8 (Mali-G715)
- **Vulkan 1.1 drivers** — GPUs whose drivers stop at Vulkan 1.1 (Valhall Mali on older or vendor-capped drivers, Qualcomm's own older drivers, early Xclipse, PowerVR BXM) run through a compatibility layer (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/compat.c`)
- **Older GPUs without descriptor indexing (experimental)** — Bifrost Mali (G71, G72, G76, G52) and PowerVR Rogue: each draw binds its own textures, and depth is clamped in the shader where the GPU can't
- **Adreno** — unchanged: every replacement is off where the GPU has the feature.

### App
- **GPU driver** — a screen of its own (Settings → GPU driver): the system driver and the stored packages in one list, with their versions and authors. Packages are checked when added and can be deleted (deleting the one in use goes back to the system driver)
- **Turnip recommended** — a Qualcomm phone running its own driver older than Vulkan 1.3 suggests a Turnip driver once, from the library
- **Back key** — the device's back key opens the in-game menu, from any input, including the Retroid Pocket 5's own Back. A controller with both Back and Select keeps Back for the menu; on one without a Select key, Back is the Xbox Back button
- **Dark theme** — Settings → Display → App theme: the phone's, light or dark; the in-game menus follow it, in the app's green rather than Android's teal
- **Controller navigation** — the app works with a controller: the focused item stands out (a game is outlined in green), A selects, B goes back, and Y or Select opens a game's menu. The search field opens the keyboard only on A, the library has a refresh button, the mapping sliders move with left and right, release notes scroll, and X deletes a savestate from the in-game Load state list

releases.name: hakuX 1.0.0
releases.body:
A new core replaces xemu's QEMU-based one.

### New core
- **CPU** — the Xbox's x86 code runs on a FEX JIT (FEXCore fork), and the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively (`native/kernel`): no QEMU
- **GPU** — the NV2A push buffer is decoded into Vulkan (HLE, `hw/xbox/hle`). Custom drivers (Turnip) load through adrenotools; driver-specific workarounds are quirks (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`, `debug.hakux.quirks`)
- **Audio** — the MCPX APU runs on the core's own services (`native/dev/apu`), out through AAudio
- **Savestates** — per game, in slots, with the hard disk's files
- **Mods and cheats** — per game, from `mods/` (library long-press "Mods & cheats"): XBE patches and replaced disc files; 60 and 120 fps mods for 13 games (`mods/README.md`, generators in `tools/mods`)
- **Controllers** — each physical controller routed to a player with its own mapping; the on-screen controller adds to player 1

### New features
- **Updates** — hakuX looks for a newer release on GitHub when it starts and on demand (Settings → Updates); one found shows its notes and installs from there
- **Frontends** — a game launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns to it when it closes
- **Console clock** — follows the phone's time and time zone, or a time set by hand (Settings → Console → Clock)
- **Start errors** — a game that can't start says why (the file can't be read, isn't an Xbox disc, or its program can't load) and goes back to the library
- **Mods** — Halo 2's 60 fps mod draws characters, vehicles and objects at 60; DOA2's 120 fps mod keeps the select screen's legend

### Performance
- **No pipeline-cache stutter** — each game keeps its own pipeline cache, written only after new compiles; the one shared by every game was rewritten every few seconds and froze the picture for 0.2–0.8 s (Ninja Gaiden Black)
- **Audio** — about 32 ms of latency instead of 128 ms, and less CPU for the sound engine
- **GPU emulation** — faster push-buffer decoding, texture unswizzling (NEON) and hashing, fewer lookups per draw
- **Savestates** — compressed on several threads (a Halo 2 save: 9.6 s to 3.9 s)
- **Idle frames** — the screen isn't redrawn when nothing changed, and the on-screen controller redraws only what changed
- **Disc reads** — a large read waits only its own thread, not the whole game
- **Library** — folders scanned in one pass (38 games: 270 ms to 63 ms)

### App
- **On-screen controller** — the menu button is a green dot
- **Large screens** — Android 16 keeps the landscape lock (the app is declared a game)
- **Storage** — JIT symbol maps left by earlier builds (gigabytes on some devices) are deleted at start
- **Backups** — hakuX's data is left out of Android's cloud backups and device transfers
- **Library** — savestate thumbnails and driver ZIPs load off the main thread

releases.name: hakuX 0.3.1
releases.body:
## hakuX v0.3.1

### Performance
- Fix significant FPS regression on "lower-end" devices (Adreno < 740)
- Proper BC3 support
- Multiple tweaks to texture cache, significant improvements on titles such as Forza Motorsport

### Bug Fixes
- Fix BC3/DXT5 texture corruption on 3D textures
- Fix XISO converter not producing valid output — replaced Rust xdvdfs with C extract-xiso

### Diagnostics
- Persistent log capture across sessions — logs survive app restart, previous session preserved

releases.name: NetherSX2-Turnip v0.7

* Default resolution changed to 2x Native
* Hardware Download Mode defaults to Disabled Readbacks (no longer warns on this setting)

releases.name: NetherSX2-Turnip v0.4
releases.body:
* Rewrote the methodology - now uses libadrenotools approach. Will now work fine on Snapdragon Elite/Later Android versions (wasn't before!)

So if it was not working for you before - it should now.
Thanks to all the testers SubhanHabib, Yuasasa and others who have helped me track down the issues on devices I do not own.

If you do see any issues - please raise an Issue and provide the logs (preferably logcat logs with logcat logging enabled in NetherSX2 (it's in the Advanced section))

releases.name: WinHub 1.2
releases.body:
# WinHub 1.2 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **WinHub 1.2 is about looks and controls.** 15 new Deck themes, a Deck-style Controls tab, OpenGL and Mods in the XMB game settings, a rebuilt fake-HDR look, and a tidier Storage tab. Unreal Engine HDR is removed. # What's New — everything since 1.1 ## 🎨 15 new Deck themes The theme picker grows from **7 to 22**. Every new theme is dark, recolours the whole app (popups and touch controls included) and shows up in **Deck Settings → Theme**, **Appearance** and the **first-run wizard**. | | Theme | Accent | Look | |---|---|---|---| | 🌊 | **Ocean** | teal `#14B8A6` | deep navy-teal surfaces | | 🟡 | **Amber** | gold `#F59E0B` | warm brown-black, a "retro handheld" feel | | 🌇 | **Sunset** | rose `#FB7185` + violet | dusky plum surfaces, violet on toggles and chips | | ❄️ | **Nord** | frost blue `#88C0D0` | muted blue-grey, low contrast and easy on the eyes | | 🌌 | **Midnight** | indigo `#6366F1` | pure-black OLED background, very dark cards | | 🎄 | **Christmas** | red `#E11D48` + green | festive pair, in the style of Halloween | | 🧛 | **Dracula** | purple `#BD93F9` + pink | the classic dark purple-grey | | 🍂 | **Gruvbox** | orange `#FE8019` | warm retro browns with cream text | | 🌅 | **Solarized** | cyan `#2AA198` + yellow | dark teal base | | 🏙️ | **Tokyo Night** | blue `#7AA2F7` | cool navy surfaces | | 🐈 | **Catppuccin** | mauve `#CBA6F7` | soft pastel on a mocha base | | 🌹 | **Rose Pine** | rose `#EBBCBA` + lilac | dusky muted pastels | | 🤖 | **Cyberpunk** | neon yellow `#FCEE0A` + cyan | black surfaces | | 🎛️ | **Synthwave** | hot pink `#FF2E97` + cyan | deep violet surfaces | | 🌲 | **Forest** | moss `#84CC16` | dark olive-brown, different from the mint Green | - 🔤 Colours from Dracula, Gruvbox, Solarized, Nord, Tokyo Night, Catppuccin and Rose Pine are *inspired by* those well-known editor palettes. - 👁️ Text on every accent is picked for readability (dark ink on Amber, Ocean, Nord, Gruvbox and the other light accents, white on the rest). - 💾 **Your theme is kept.** The new themes were added before the hidden Custom slot, and a one-time remap makes sure anyone on **Custom** stays on Custom. ## 🎮 Deck-style Controls tab The Controls tab now looks and navigates like the rest of Deck mode instead of Material cards. - 🧱 **New layout:** a header, a rail (chips in portrait), a **Profile** group and Deck rows and buttons replace the Material cards and segmented tabs. - 🔁 **One index:** sections are driven by the Deck tab host, so **L1 / R1** and the rail always agree on which section is open. - 💬 **Deck dialogs and menus:** name prompts, confirmations, the import chooser, the profile download list and the layout preview all use the Deck dialog and Deck buttons. Profile and copy menus use the Deck colours. - 👥 **Assign tab:** each player slot is now a **Deck choice row**. The container and shortcut editors keep their existing slot editor unchanged. - 🖼️ A design mockup for the tab was added under `docs/`. ## 🕹️ XMB game settings: OpenGL and Mods Two things that existed in the pop-up and Deck game editors were missing from the XMB (the PSP-style game menu, landscape and portrait). They are there now: pick a game, then **Settings**. **Graphics → OpenGL** ⚡ - ⚡ **Fast OpenGL**, 📊 **Show OpenGL FPS** and 🔓 **OpenGL vsync off**, each **Auto / On / Off** where Auto follows the container (and says what it would be, e.g. *Auto (On)*). - 🔒 Fast OpenGL greys out, with the reason, when the game's driver isn't a Turnip or this build has no X11 GL set. **Mods** 🧩 (a new section after Controller) - 🧩 **Game mods:** a switch for each mod the game's EXE can take (**REFramework** for RE Engine games, **Special K** for 32 and 64-bit Windows games). Switching one on downloads it the first time, with its state shown (*Downloading…*, *ready*, *download failed*). - 🏷️ **Special K DLL name:** pick the name it loads as, or leave it on *(auto)*. - ▶️ **Start with the game:** add programs by Windows path (a trainer, for example), then open one to change its path or **wait before starting**, move it **up or down**, or remove it. The first waits from the game launching, each next one after the one before it starts. - ✅ Everything is saved to the game's settings straight away, the same way the pop-up editor does it. Section list: General · Graphics · Win Components · Env Vars · Advanced · Controller · **Mods** · TV. ## 🌈 A better fake-HDR look The in-game **HDR** toggle is still the same one-tap on/off, but the effect behind it is rewritten. - ☀️ **Highlights only.** It works in linear light, lifts just the bright areas and adds a soft highlight-only bloom, instead of a gamma-space curve that clipped highlights and muddied colours. - 🎞️ **Soft shoulder.** Everything rolls off smoothly under SDR white, so nothing clips. - 🎨 **Depth and colour.** Mids and darks get a touch more depth and a small saturation boost, kept back in bright areas so they don't over-saturate. - 📏 **Same on any screen:** the glow is sized in pixels scaled to the picture, so it looks the same at any resolution. - 🛡️ **Safe by design:** it is still SDR in and SDR out. The display never switches mode and nothing about the swapchain changes. It is a nicer "HDR look", not real HDR, so it can't go brighter than SDR white. ## 🗄️ Storage tab - 🍷 **Container icon.** Containers in **Storage** and in the **add-game container picker** now show the same wine-glass container icon as the Containers tab, tinted with your Deck theme colour so it follows every theme. - 🧬 **Cronos containers stay in the Cronos tab.** Containers made by the Cronos add-game flow are now tagged and listed **only** in the **Cronos** tab. They no longer appear in the **Containers** tab or in the **Master Containers** pickers. Older single-game containers are tagged automatically the first time you open Storage. - 🎯 **Per-button focus rings.** On Storage and Saves cards, the ring now lights up the exact button you are on instead of the whole card, so a D-pad always shows where you are. ## 🛒 Stores and Home - 🔥 **Featured on Steam.** A new row on the **Stores** page (landscape picker and portrait list) shows Steam's featured titles. Tap one to open its store page. Nothing shows until the catalog answers, so there is never an empty box. - 👋 **Home greeting.** Portrait Home now says **Good morning / Good afternoon / Good evening** in place of "WinHub". - 🎮 **Stores L2 / R2.** Stores reports its pages to the Deck shell, so **L2 / R2** page through it without relying on Compose focus. ## 🔄 Update check - ⏱️ The update check on app open no longer hashes the installed APK, which made it time out and wrongly report "no update". - 🥇 It now runs **first**, before the background step, and always tells you the result: **Update available**, **No updates found** or **Couldn't check for updates**. ## 🗑️ Removed: Unreal Engine HDR The *Unreal Engine HDR* setting (Off / DirectX 12 fix / DirectX 11 NVAPI) is gone from the project. - ❌ Removed from the game settings, the XMB and the launch path, along with the bundled **dxvk-nvapi** and its download step in the build. - 🧹 Old `unrealHdr` entries in saved containers and shortcuts are simply ignored. - ℹ️ A prefix that ever ran the DirectX 11 mode keeps its two nvapi files. Nothing loads them any more, so they are harmless. ## 🔧 Smaller - 🔢 **Version 1.2, versionCode 92.** - 🧪 Fake-HDR shader (`hdr.frag`) rewritten and its SPIR-V (`hdr_frag.h`) regenerated. - 🎨 15 presets added to `ThemePreset.kt`; a `preset_schema_v4` migration keeps Custom pointing at the right slot. - 🧩 New `XmbSettingsPhase2Mods.kt` for the XMB Mods section; the delay and program-name helpers of the Start programs editor are shared with it. - 🧰 Removed `core/UnrealHdr`, `core/DxvkNvapi`, `GpuSpoof.isNvidia` and the `dxvk-nvapi` assets and CI fetch. - 📚 The README now links to the **Telegram** and **Discord** communities. ## ⚠️ Carried over — still open - Nothing from 1.1 is known to be fixed by this release. Hermes and Fast OpenGL are still the likeliest places to find bugs.
📦 Where to get Proton 9 (tap to expand) The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog.
📜 Every change since 1.1 — 25 merged, oldest first - Add Telegram and Discord links to README · [`49b7bae3`](https://github.com/winhub-emu/winhub/commit/49b7bae3c4f5f4e4384c9177a0cbe8bd240ecd88) - Cozy landscape restyle (softer shapes, no card outlines, Bricolage font) · [`61c4f6ba`](https://github.com/winhub-emu/winhub/commit/61c4f6ba9705182fbb6deb658b2951235346ba32) - releases.name: WinHub 1.1
releases.body:
> If you want to post this on Reddit (specifically r/EmulationOnAndroid), please include an AI Disclaimer, otherwise your post **will** be removed. # WinHub 1.1 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **WinHub 1.1 is about first impressions and logs.** A first-run setup wizard for fresh installs, and a Deck-style Log Manager, log viewer and Report a problem dialog. > ⚠️ **The setup wizard is new in this release.** If the first install misbehaves, report it with the new Report a problem dialog. # What's New — everything since 1.0 ## 🧭 First-run setup wizard A fresh install no longer starts downloading straight away. WinHub first walks you through a five-step wizard, then installs everything behind the usual setup overlay. - 🪜 **Five steps, one progress bar:** Layout → Theme → Contents → Social Hub → Install, with a "STEP n OF 5" header and a step strip so you always know where you are. - 📐 **Layout.** *How do you play?* Choose **Landscape** (the Deck home with its rail) or **Portrait** (one hand on a phone: chips replace the rail, big touch targets). A live preview shows the Deck home in the layout you pick. Change it any time in **Settings → App Orientation**. - 🎨 **Theme.** *Pick your look.* The whole app, including the wizard itself, follows the theme as you try them. Change it any time in Settings. - 📦 **Contents.** The same browser as the Contents tab, with a checkbox per release, search, and family → repository → release navigation. **Proton 9 arm64ec, DXVK 2.4.1 gplasync, FEXCore 2610 PPA unix and VKD3D 3.0.1 are always installed** and carry an **Included** badge. Tick anything else you want now, or add it later from Contents. - 💬 **Social Hub.** *Connect to Social Hub* with GitHub (device code: open the link on any device and enter the code). Shows *Connected as you* when done, or **Not now** to skip and connect later from the Social tab. It explains what you get: import configs in one tap, share your own, and join in with posts, replies and votes. Sign-in problems show a message and a **Try again**. - ⬇️ **Install.** An **Install plan** lists every item (system files, the four included components and your extras), the item count, and a reminder that it needs an internet connection and Wi-Fi is recommended. - 📊 **Setup overlay.** The install list now shows each chosen extra as its own row, and scrolls so a long list never pushes the button off screen. The progress is split into equal slices, one for the system files and one per component. - 🎮 **Controller first.** **A** selects, **B** goes back a step, **LB / RB** switch steps, with on-screen button hints in the footer. Back and Next / Install buttons work by touch too. - 🔁 **Only on a fresh install.** Updates that only need a newer ImageFS skip the wizard, and it only runs once. - 🛠️ **Fix: Deck follows your layout.** Deck reads the orientation preference once when it starts, and it used to start behind the wizard, so picking Portrait left it on the landscape layout rotated upright. The shell is now held back until the wizard finishes, and the shown orientation is saved even if you never tap a choice. - 🔒 The permission prompts wait until you tap **Proceed**, so nothing interrupts the wizard. ## 🗂️ Deck-style Log Manager In Deck mode, Settings now opens a themed Log Manager instead of the classic dialog. It uses the same preferences and log inventory as before, so nothing you set is lost. - 💾 **Storage meter** at the top showing how much space logs use, and the folder logs are saved to. - 🔀 **Four sections:** **Capture**, **Storage**, **Game logs** and **Tools**. Switch with **LB / RB**. - 🎙️ **Capture.** Switches for Wine debug (with a channel picker and *Browse all channels*), DXVK and VKD3D logs, **Controller input**, SteamLite, **Android logcat**, **Crash reports** and **Exit reasons** (auto-save on launch, Android 11+). Each has a short plain-language hint about what it costs, and an **ⓘ** that explains it. - 📁 **Where logs go.** Log location (default, custom folder or *Choose folder…*), **Folder for each game**, and **Keep last** (how many runs to keep, or no history). - 🧹 **Storage.** Total size, **Clear all** (with a confirmation that only files WinHub wrote are removed) and a **Biggest folders** list, with a delete confirmation for the app and crash logs. - 🎮 **Game logs.** Every game's logs in one place, with a helpful empty state: *Turn on a log in Capture, then launch a game.* - 🧰 **Tools.** **Capture logcat now**, **Read last crash** (why Android ended the app last time, saved with your logs), the **Native engines** switches (Rust engine for Epic, GOG and Amazon downloads), a **Store download speed** ceiling, and **Explain the log types**. - 🎮 **Controller friendly** with focus rings on every row and action. ## 🔍 Deck-style log viewer - 🎨 Opens in the **Deck palette** from the Deck Log Manager, with 44dp actions and clear focus rings. - 🔎 **Find**, **Copy** and **Share** actions along the bottom, plus a follow switch for live logs. - 🔗 A shortcut's **View logs** opens the same Deck viewer when you are in Deck mode. - 🧱 The classic Log Manager and viewer are unchanged when Deck mode is off, and the shortcut editor still uses the classic look. ## 📝 Report a problem - 🪟 Now a **Deck dialog with controller-editable fields**: *What went wrong?* and *Details* (optional). - 📎 A **Will be attached** list shows exactly which logs go into the report, with a toggle to also include the app logcat and crash reports. - 🔐 The report is saved as a **zip in Downloads**. E-mail addresses, auth tokens and your Steam account name are stripped; file paths are kept so they stay useful, so glance over them if a folder name identifies you. - 🌐 **Continue on GitHub** opens a prefilled issue. GitHub can't take a file from a link, so attach the zip with the paperclip once the form opens. If there is no browser, you get a clear message instead of a crash. - ⚡ Building the report runs off the main thread, with a *Working…* state on the button. ## 🔧 Smaller - ⏱️ The release workflow now **times out the patches job after 15 minutes**, so a hung flavor cannot hold up a release. A flavor that times out just ships full-size updates without `.wh` patches. - 🧩 The Contents browser pieces (category cards, badges, icons) are shared between the Contents tab and the wizard, instead of copied. - 📚 Release notes use the WinHub logo, and the default repo for release notes is `winhub-emu/winhub`. ## ⚠️ Carried over — still open - Nothing from 1.0 is known to be fixed by this release. Hermes and Fast OpenGL are still the likeliest places to find bugs.
📦 Where to get Proton 9 (tap to expand) The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog.

releases.body:
# WinHub 1.0 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **WinHub 1.0 is about controllers, the HUD and OpenGL.** A brand new controller engine (Hermes) with real hot-plug, rumble and Direct XInput, a rebuilt Fusion HUD, Fast OpenGL through Mesa + Zink, a Sync selector, a Music Player and a lot of portrait and Deck polish. > ⚠️ **Hermes and Fast OpenGL are new in this release.** If a controller or an OpenGL game misbehaves, turn the setting off for that container or game and report it. # What's New — everything since 0.1 ## 🎮 Hermes controller engine A new way to get your controller into the game, replacing the old shared-memory ring. - 🪽 One fixed-size shared state file per player slot. A button pressed and released between two reads is still delivered, both the press and the release. - 🔌 Real hot-plug, live reconnect of held slots, and the on-screen pad is seated before Wine boots. - 🆔 Per-slot controller identity and DirectInput force feedback. - 🧩 **Direct XInput:** replacement `xinput` DLLs (x86_64, i386, ARM64X) per container, with in-game switching and rumble. - 🕐 Stick updates paced to the game's frame rate: Auto, Fixed or Unpaced. - 🧪 New **Controls → Pad** tab in the in-game menu, and a **Controller input** log in the Log Manager. - 🔀 *Enable XInput*, *Enable DInput* and *Exclusive Input* became one switch: **"DirectInput games can see the controller"**. Old data reads the same. - 🆕 New containers start with Direct XInput on and the DirectInput switch off. Existing containers keep their own settings. > ⚠️ New in 1.0. Please report controller problems. ## 📊 Fusion HUD, rebuilt - 🧱 Four Steam Deck style levels: FPS, + frametime graph, + GPU/CPU/memory, everything. - 🎨 MangoHud colours, a big FPS number that turns amber and red as it drops, per-core bars. - ⏱️ Level 4 shows a **PRES** row (present latency and skipped frames) while SurfaceDirect runs. - 🗑️ The Classic, GameHub and GameNative HUDs are gone. A saved HUD style of another value becomes Fusion. New containers start at level 2. ## 🚀 Fast OpenGL - OpenGL games present through the bundled Mesa + Zink over a Vulkan swapchain instead of a readback on every frame. - EGL layers take the EGL route. Others use a new opt-in server-side GLX. - **Show FPS** and **Vsync off** switches sit beside it, in the container editors and as Auto / On / Off per game. > ⚠️ New in 1.0. The GLX route is opt-in. ## ⏲️ Sync selector Choose **esync, ntsync, fsync or wineserver** per container, or per game. Options the Wine layer cannot run are greyed out and fall back to the layer default. ## 🎵 Music Player Settings → General: pick an MP3 and play it in the app. A separate **Play in games** switch is off by default. It loops, pauses when the app leaves the screen and takes no audio focus. ## 📱 Portrait and Deck polish - 🌊 Liquid waves on Storage, Files, Controls, Contents, Saves, Social Hub, Settings and Stores. Drifting glows stay on Home. - 🏷️ A store logo or folder badge on each game cover. - 🌫️ Content fades out above the bottom bar instead of a hard cut. - 🃏 The classic game menu and small Contents dialogs are centered rounded cards. - ✏️ Text fields get a full rounded outline, with symmetric margins on text rows and Env Var values. ## 🔧 Smaller - 🛠️ Fixed a compile error in the GLX extension and a missing brace in the on-screen pad seating. - 🚫 No wave backdrop behind the per-game settings editor. - 📖 README rewritten for WinHub, version bumped to 1.0 (`versionCode 90`). ## ⚠️ Carried over — still open - Nothing from 0.1-beta is known to be fixed by this release. The new Hermes controller engine and Fast OpenGL have had limited testing, so treat them as the likeliest places to find bugs.
📦 Where to get Proton 9 (tap to expand) The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog.

releases.name: WinHub - Early Preview
releases.body: # 📜 WinHub - Early Preview ## 🚀 Version 0.1-beta > This page covers everything new in this release, grouped by what you will actually notice. 🚀 **Jump to:** [🎨 New UI](#-a-fully-revamped-ui) · [🖼️ Renderers](#️-new-renderers-egl-and-surfacedirect) · [💬 Social Hub & Game Configs](#-social-hub-and-game-configs) · [🟢 Mali](#-new-mali-support) · [🧩 Mod Loader](#-mod-loader) · [🔄 Updater](#-updater) · [🛠️ Other improvements](#️-other-improvements) · [🗑️ Removed](#️-removed) · [🙏 Credits](#-credits) --- ## 🎨 A fully revamped UI WinHub now looks and feels like a console. Everything was rebuilt around a **Deck-style shell** that works fully with a gamepad **and** with touch, in landscape **and** in portrait. ### 🕹️ The Deck shell (landscape) - 🏠 **Console-style Home.** A top-left carousel of your games with big glowing covers, a launch zoom when you press play, a blurred cover backdrop, a status strip, a details panel, an intro, and L2/R2 to switch shelves (**All, Recent, Favourites, Store games**). - 🎛️ **Two Home styles** (Settings → Appearance): **XMB** (default) with the game options column, and **Classic**, which opens a full console-style game menu when you hold a cover or press **Y**. - 🧭 **Hint bar, Start quick menu, download tray, idle screensaver and a sound set**, so the whole app reacts like a console. - 🔁 **Shoulder buttons switch things the same way everywhere.** L1/R1 move between sections, L2/R2 move between sub-tabs, **A** selects, **B** goes back and never exits the app by accident. - 🌊 **Stretchy tab pills and a gliding focus ring** that follows your D-pad across grids, lists, buttons and dialogs. Rings hide after you touch the screen. - ⌨️ **A-to-edit text fields**, so a controller never gets stuck inside a keyboard field. - 🪟 **Full-screen Deck dialogs** with controller navigation, plus warning popups for backup and restore. ### 📱 Portrait mode, built from scratch - 🫧 **Liquid Home.** Soft glows drift behind the page and three layers of waves roll along the bottom. Colours follow your theme. - 🔮 **Glass cards** for the Continue Playing banner, the Add game tile and shelf chips. - 🎮 **Continue playing banner** that floats gently and jumps straight back into your last game. - 💊 **Floating, rounded bottom bar** with every section as an icon and label tab. - 👆 **Hold a game cover to open its menu**, with a little haptic tick. Tap it to open the game page (banner, stats, Play, Settings, Options, About). - 🕘 **Home header** with the clock and your Social Hub avatar. - 📚 Settings, Contents, the container editor and Storage use a **top Deck tab strip with icons**, or a category list if you prefer (Settings → Appearance → Portrait Tabs). - 🏪 **Stores page** with each store's real logo and brand colours. ### 🎨 Themes - 🌈 **Seven themes** (including a new blue **Azure**) with a live theme picker. - 🧩 The in-game drawer, launch banner and portrait page all follow the active theme, light or dark. ### 🧰 Editors rebuilt for the Deck - 📦 **Container editor** in three layouts (**tabs, side rail or category pages**), split into labelled sections, with inline config panels and a structured **Env Vars** editor. - 🎯 **Shortcut (per-game) editor** rebuilt Deck-native: General, Graphics, Win Components, Env Vars, Advanced, Controller, **Mods**, plus TV when a display is connected. Wrapper Manager, Audio, Performance and download sheets are all Deck-native. - 🧮 **Presets editable in Settings.** Box64 and FEXCore presets can now be added, edited, duplicated, deleted, exported and imported from Settings → General. - ⚙️ **Custom startup services.** Choosing **Custom** under Startup Selection now shows a switch for every Wine service, in both the container and the shortcut editor. - 🚀 **Launch method picker** (SteamLite, Goldberg, Raw) in the game menu and shortcut editor. ### 🛒 Stores - 🏬 **Steam, Epic, GOG, Amazon and Xbox** all share the same Deck tab strip (Store, Library, Profile). - 🟩 **Xbox store**, including an in-Deck install screen with a PC package picker, store tabs, downloads and a cloud-gaming Stream launch method. - ⭐ Store pages show **Metacritic and How Long To Beat**, with richer game details and Steam achievements. - 🏷️ Your library tags each game by store, and hand-added games are tagged **Custom**. ### 🕹️ In-game menu - 🪟 **Console-style quick menu.** A right-docked glass panel with a header of quick tiles, a tab rail and a **Quick** landing page, fully controller-navigable. - 🧩 New **Mods** tab in the drawer (see [Mod Loader](#-mod-loader)). - 🫥 Transparent in-game menu controls, with option groups in one rounded outline. ### 🧼 First run and polish - 🛠️ **WinHub setup screen** and a one-time **launch screen** that brings the store services online. - 🖼️ New app icons. - 🪄 **Launch banner** with an *Update available* message that never waits more than five seconds on the update check. - 📂 **File manager and Saves** have location pills and a Deck look. Pickers use the Deck file manager in portrait or landscape. - 🧠 Shared Wine base prefix through a copy-on-write overlay, so each container is only a thin skeleton on disk. --- ## 🖼️ New renderers: EGL and SurfaceDirect A **renderer** is the part of WinHub that takes the game's window and puts it on your screen. WinHub now has three, and you can choose per container **and** per game: ### 🔷 Vulkan (unchanged) The existing renderer. Draws windows with Vulkan and keeps all its current options. ### 🟦 EGL (new) - 🧠 **What it does:** an **OpenGL ES** renderer. A native render thread mirrors the X server's windows, cursors and pointer and draws them with OpenGL ES. - ⚡ **Why it's good:** window contents are stored in **AHardwareBuffer** memory and sampled **without copying**. DXVK and VKD3D games can hand their finished frames straight to it through the Present extension. - 🎯 **Pick it when:** your GPU's Vulkan driver is unreliable for presenting, or you want the simplest, most compatible path. - 🛟 **Safe fallback:** if the native side can't start, WinHub falls back to Vulkan by itself. - ⚙️ **Settings:** none. EGL needs no tuning, so its renderer settings row is hidden. ### 🟪 SurfaceDirect (new) - 🧠 **What it does:** hands each X window to **Android's SurfaceFlinger** as its own **SurfaceControl layer** that shows the game's frame buffer directly. Android's compositor does the final combine in hardware, so WinHub does **no extra GPU composition pass**. - ⚡ **Why it's good:** the shortest route from the game's frame to the display, which means lower overhead and less latency on supported devices. - 🎚️ **Settings:** - 🚀 **Performance mode** - 🔄 **Present at refresh rate** - 📤 **Submit every buffer** - 🎯 **Precise presentation** - 🛟 **Safe fallback:** needs Android 10 or newer. On older versions WinHub falls back to Vulkan. > NOTE: This SurfaceDirect is not our latest one, it is still the very first one that was made. The actual, latest SurfaceDirect will be released in 1.0. > ❤️ **SurfaceDirect is a fork of DisplayX by [PissBlaster649](https://github.com/Pipetto-crypto)**, thanks to him in the first place. Each renderer now only shows **its own** settings in the Deck, classic and XMB editors, so you never see options that don't apply. --- ## 💬 Social Hub and Game Configs The **Social Hub** is a built-in community space, now with two sub-tabs and your own profile. It runs on GitHub Issues in `winhub-emu/social-hub`, so there is nothing extra to install. ### 📰 Feed - ✍️ Post, comment, search, refresh. A post is a GitHub issue and a comment is an issue comment. - 🖼️ Add pictures, which are uploaded and embedded in the post. - 🗑️ Deleting your own post hides it (GitHub has no true delete for non-owners). - 🔐 Sign in with GitHub inside the app. ### 🎮 Game Configurations Share the exact settings you use for a game, and import other people's in one tap. - 📤 **Upload** a game's config from your library with an optional note. It carries the container and shortcut settings, **plus a record of which repository each component (driver, DXVK, VKD3D, wrapper...) came from**. - 📥 **Import** a config in one tap. WinHub fetches each component **from that exact source**, asks you to pick the game's `.exe`, and sets the shortcut up. - 🔍 **Search** configs by game name. - 📱 **Matches my device** filter shows only configs from phones like yours (same SoC and GPU). - 👍 **Like** and 💬 **reply** to config threads so the good ones rise to the top. - 🧭 Works with the controller (L2/R2 or LB/RB switch sub-tabs) and follows your layout setting (rail, tabs or pages). ### 🌍 Community Configs In a game's menu you can also browse the **community config index**. It's cached on the device, loads instantly after the first fetch, works offline, and falls back to a clean empty state instead of an error. ### 🙋 Profile Pick a **custom display name and picture**. It's stored on a hidden profiles issue and shown across the feed and the Home header. --- ## 🟢 New Mali support WinHub now has real support for **Arm Mali and Immortalis GPUs**, which many phones use. Everything below only turns on for Mali. **Adreno phones behave exactly as before.** 🧑‍🔧 *These features are new and Mali is hard to test everywhere, so please report what works and what doesn't.* ### 🔍 Detection and the force switch - 🧭 **Force Mali mode** (Settings → General). Turn this on if the app doesn't detect a non-Adreno GPU. It makes every Mali option available on any GPU. ### 📥 Drivers - 🧱 **PanVK driver sources.** On Mali, the driver download list shows three PanVK feeds first: **PanVK-kbase (Mali)**, **FristOneRR PanVK (Mali)** and **PanVK G615**. PanVK is the open-source Vulkan driver for Mali. - 🧪 **Newer compat layer.** The Mali compat layer (used by the *Wrapper + compat + bcn* driver on Valhall Mali) is updated to leegao's `22960fb3`, adding an immutable-YCbCr fallback, fake `maintenance5` and calibrated-timestamps handling. Existing containers re-extract it once. ### 🖼️ Textures - 🚀 **Faster BCn layer (Fcharan build).** An opt-in checkbox in the graphics driver dialog. It swaps the bundled BCn texture decoder for a faster build with the same memory use, which helps with slow texture loading and stutter. It's only offered where the BCn layer actually runs. ### 🎛️ PanVK tuning In the graphics driver dialog, a **Mali (PanVK) driver** section: - 🧮 **PANVK_HEAP_MB** (256–16384): the driver's heap size. - 🧮 **PANVK_TILER_HEAP_MB** (16–2048) and **PANVK_POLY_HEAP_MB** (4–512): the tiler and polygon heaps. - 🔢 **PANVK_ATOM_STRIDE** (Auto, 56 or 64). - 🪵 **PANVK_TRACE**: driver tracing for bug reports. - 🙈 **Hide present-wait / dynamic-rendering extensions.** Hides `present_id`, `present_wait` and `dynamic_rendering` from the game and turns on *Disable present wait*, for freezes and black screens on PanVK. Out-of-range values are simply not used. ### 📊 HUD - 📈 **GPU usage and clock from hardware counters** for CSF-generation Mali (Mali-G310, G510, G610, G615, G710, G715, G720, G925 and Immortalis). It reads the kernel driver's counters and needs no root, and it's used only when the usual sysfs paths are blocked. - 📟 **MediaTek GPU-load and Pixel/Tensor voltage fallbacks**, for phones that block the standard GPU nodes. ### 🖥️ X11 renderer - ⏱️ **High-priority GPU queue** on Mali so WinHub's own frame work doesn't wait behind a GPU-bound game. - 🧾 **Valid AHB import format.** The Android hardware-buffer image format is now correct for Mali drivers. ### 🧠 Emulation - 🧬 Two new **FEXCore presets**: **Unreal Engine 3** (all TSO options on, reduced x87 precision, multiblock off) and **Performance (full x87)** for games whose physics break under reduced precision. - 🛡️ **Registry fix.** A Wine registry key that can't be written no longer crashes the app. > 💚 **Mali work by [The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner)**, built on WinlatorMali by GunaCharanTeja, leegao's compat layer and BCn layer, FristOneRR's PanVK driver and the PanVK-kbase project. --- ## 🧩 Mod Loader A new per-game **mod loader** adds popular game mods without touching your game files by hand. ### 📚 Where to find it - ⚙️ **Game settings → Mods** tab, with a switch for every mod your game's EXE can take. Mods are **off by default**. - 🎮 **In-game drawer → Mods** tab, with a card for each mod and a button to show or hide its menu. ### 🦖 REFramework - 🎯 The modding framework for **RE Engine games** (Resident Evil 2/3/4/7/8/9, Devil May Cry 5, Monster Hunter Rise/Wilds/Stories 3, Street Fighter 6, Dragon's Dogma 2, Onimusha, Pragmata and more). It only appears for those EXEs and for 64-bit. - 🧱 An **ARM64EC build** that skips x86-64 inline hooks on ARM64EC code (fixing the "illegal instruction" crash), opens its menu with **L3 + R3** on a controller, works in games whose DirectInput blocks key messages (RE2), no longer hangs at startup, and keeps the game's cursor hidden while it draws its own, so you see one cursor. - 📂 Placed as `dinput8.dll`, with `dinput8=n,b` merged into your DLL overrides (**your own entries are kept**). Its menu starts closed. - ⌨️ Drawer menu button sends **Insert**. ### ✨ Special K - 🔭 The popular overlay and tweak tool for almost any game. Works with 32-bit and 64-bit EXEs. - 🏷️ Placed under the right graphics name: `dxgi.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, `d3d9.dll`, `d3d8.dll` or `opengl32.dll`, **picked automatically from the EXE's imports**, or chosen by you per game. - 🤝 Works together with REFramework, and closing its panel no longer freezes the game. - ⌨️ Drawer menu button sends **Ctrl + Shift + Backspace**. ### 🛡️ How it stays safe - 🌐 Mods are **downloaded the first time you switch one on**, not bundled. This keeps the app smaller. - ✅ Each download is checked against its **size and SHA-256** and cached once per device. - 🏷️ A small **marker file** records exactly what was placed, so WinHub only ever replaces or removes **its own** file. A DLL your game already ships is **never touched**. - 📋 Every step is written to the session log. ### 🚦 Start programs with the game (trainers, Cheat Engine) - ➕ **Add any number of programs** to start when a game launches, such as a FLiNG trainer or Cheat Engine. - ⏱️ **Set a wait for each one.** The first waits after the game launches. Each next one waits after the previous one starts. Pick from *Right away* to 5 minutes (for example, "launch, wait 5 s, launch the next"). - 🔀 **Arrange button.** Opens the whole list so you can reorder it. Pick a program up, tap where it should go (or press **Up/Down**), tap again to drop it. **Remove** takes the picked one out. - ▶️ **Start button in the drawer** for each program, to run it again mid-game. - 📁 Programs start **from their own folder**, using a small batch file, so long paths work. - 🧵 **Long Task Manager commands work now.** Commands longer than the helper accepts (51 bytes) used to fail silently, and now go through the same batch-file route. > 💜 **Mod Loader work by [The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner)**, with REFramework by praydog and Special K by Kaldaien and the SpecialKO contributors. --- ## 🔄 Updater - 📡 **Updater tab in Settings** with a **Stable / Preview** channel switch. - 🪶 **Small updates.** Instead of the full APK you can download a compact patch (`.wh`) built against your installed version. - ⬇️ **Download and install button** in Settings → Updates when an update is available. - 🏷️ Releases and their `update.json` are published from `winhub-emu/winhub`. - 🔒 Downloads are verified by SHA-256 before installing. --- ## 🛠️ Other improvements - ⚡ **Lower overhead.** The performance HUD only updates the overlay you can see, and the X server no longer polls `/proc` or busy-spins at launch. - 🎮 **Controller reliability.** Focus lands on the first control after a tab switch, drag rings no longer stick or balloon, and the app reads the D-pad/stick hat axes properly. - 🧩 **Per-game launch fixes.** A game in a Master container edits its own shortcut, the saved container is used at launch, and container save failures now show a message instead of failing silently. - 🪄 **Frame generation fixes.** A per-game *Off* now inherits the container's LSFG setting properly, and picking LSFG in the Deck editor no longer saves as *Off*. - 🧾 **Driver and DXVK versions** no longer revert to defaults when you save. - 🪟 **Hide Vulkan-only options** on devices without Vulkan. - 🗃️ **Storage page** shows sizes, with a Cronos/Containers split and remove actions. - 🧰 **GitHub workflows** and repository links now point to `winhub-emu/winhub`. --- ## 🗑️ Removed To keep WinHub focused and stable, these were retired: - 🐧 The **Linux (gamescope) runtime**. Every session is now Wine on X11. - 🌊 The **embedded Wayland compositor** and its capture paths. - 🧱 Wayland and bionic-fg **from every selection list** (native LSFG frame generation stays). - 🏛️ The **classic Material launcher UI**. WinHub is Deck-only now. --- ## 🙏 Credits | Who | For | |---|---| | **[The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner)** 💚 | The **Mali support**, **Mod Loader** features and **Hermes** controller support foundation.| | **praydog** | [REFramework](https://github.com/praydog/REFramework) (MIT) | | **Kaldaien and the SpecialKO contributors** | [Special K](https://github.com/SpecialKO/SpecialK) (GPL-3.0) | | **GunaCharanTeja** | WinlatorMali, the source of the Mali HUD counters, the faster BCn build, FEX presets and the registry fix | | **leegao** | The Mali compat layer and the BCn layer (MIT) | | **FristOneRR** | The PanVK driver for Mali | | **Phobos** | Thoughts on the UI and how to make it better, Metacritic, SurfaceDirect help | | **Abu Nashmi** | XMB work | Thank you to everyone who tested, reported bugs and shared configs. 💙

# CronyX v3 

## 🆕 New Features

- CronyFG — experimental own native frame generation engine.

- Screen Stretch slider (0–100%) in screen effects — smooth stretching instead of hard full-stretch.

- Removed forced sharpening when stretching — effects are now controlled only from the effects menu.

- In-game virtual buttons editor over the running game: add/move/delete, change theme, assign keys — without leaving the game.

- New MangoHud-style FPS counter theme available for selection.

- Fixed horizontal FPS counter mode — it now uses the full screen width.

- Move a game to another container with automatic save transfer via the ludusavi index (20k+ games) and an option to manually pick the save folder.

- Auto-search for .exe files in Downloads folders — import your apps in one tap.

- Smart game title detection taken from Bannerlator (steam_appid, GOG manifests, exe PE metadata) with SteamGridDB cover matching.

- 9 on-screen button styles from WinNative (Glass, Shadow, Slate, Halo, Glint, Reticle, Neon, Lumina…) + a palette of 10 accent colors; old .icp profiles load without migration.

- Custom Box64/FEX environment variables in Settings: applied as defaults in the custom preset editor.

- New Glass UI design system.

- Fixed PiP mode: after leaving picture-in-picture the image was pixelated (swapchain stayed at PiP-window size) — the size is now restored.

- Reworked external mouse capture — the cursor no longer leaves the screen.

- **Winlator Bionic** — https://github.com/Pipetto-crypto/winlator

- Shortcuts screen — game version from EXE (PEParser — VS_VERSION_INFO, 12 metadata fields), green version badge, "About game" dialog, playtime and launch count on cards
- Steam library redesign — Downloads/Steam tabs, Grid/Compact/Rows views, auto accents and initials on covers, new download cards (percent/speed/ETA), animated buttons
- FPS counter — added display styles (Winlator Ludashi and GameNative)

- Effects: removed the FSR effect

- Vulkan effects: full-res offscreen buffer (swapchain size), fixed small-screen bug
- New Steam store: home/detail/search/catalog/news screens, prices/platforms/metascore, search suggest, full-text search with filters (jsoup)
- Steam library: content filter menu with counts, dedupe by appId
- Steam: fixed launch paths (workingDir/exe dir), download stall watchdog
- Steam cloud: conflict dialog, achievements overlay/watcher, workshop mod paths, save snapshot archives + launch/exit sync, CDN ranking, speed presets
- Wrappers: bundled catalog, resume downloads, tar install, reworked manager + dialog

releases.name: CronyX v3
releases.body:
# CronyX v3 

## 🆕 New Features

- CronyFG — experimental own native frame generation engine.

- Screen Stretch slider (0–100%) in screen effects — smooth stretching instead of hard full-stretch.

- Removed forced sharpening when stretching — effects are now controlled only from the effects menu.

- In-game virtual buttons editor over the running game: add/move/delete, change theme, assign keys — without leaving the game.

- New MangoHud-style FPS counter theme available for selection.

- Fixed horizontal FPS counter mode — it now uses the full screen width.

- Move a game to another container with automatic save transfer via the ludusavi index (20k+ games) and an option to manually pick the save folder.

- Auto-search for .exe files in Downloads folders — import your apps in one tap.

- Smart game title detection taken from Bannerlator (steam_appid, GOG manifests, exe PE metadata) with SteamGridDB cover matching.

- 9 on-screen button styles from WinNative (Glass, Shadow, Slate, Halo, Glint, Reticle, Neon, Lumina…) + a palette of 10 accent colors; old .icp profiles load without migration.

- Custom Box64/FEX environment variables in Settings: applied as defaults in the custom preset editor.

- New Glass UI design system.

- Fixed PiP mode: after leaving picture-in-picture the image was pixelated (swapchain stayed at PiP-window size) — the size is now restored.

- Reworked external mouse capture — the cursor no longer leaves the screen.

****Thanks to these projects — some features were taken from and implemented based on their code:****

- **Winlator Bionic** — https://github.com/Pipetto-crypto/winlator
- **Bannerlator** — https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator
- **WinNative** — https://github.com/WinNative-Emu/WinNative
- **GameNative** — https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative
- **Winlator Ludashi** — https://github.com/StevenMXZ/Winlator-Ludashi

<details>
<summary>← Click here to view full previous changelog</summary>

### Previous Major Updates

- New loading screen for containers
- Big Picture mode
- Update checker — automatic GitHub release check on startup, dialog with "What's new" notes, APK download with progress, installation, "Skip version"
- **Wine registry editor** — tab in container settings: key tree with search, value editing, .reg import/export
- Container exit screen — return to menu without process restart, async cleanup without UI freeze
- New **Customization** section:
  → 13 theme presets (OLED, cyberpunk, dracula, matrix, etc.), System/Light/Dark mode, Material You, custom color via ColorPicker (HSV+HEX)
  → UI/font scale, corner radius, theme export/import as JSON
  → Wallpapers: image/GIF/video, blur/darken, adjust screen (pinch/pan, separate portrait and landscape), surface transparency
  → Screen transition animations: 7 styles (fade/slide/zoom/scale...), duration 100–600 ms
  → X-Server menu: hide unused in-game menu items via checkboxes
- Controls editor fully migrated to Compose — panel with Undo/Redo, Quick Add (13 ready-made bindings), element settings (scale/opacity/rotation/color/icon), key picker (keyboard/mouse/gamepad with 16 zones)
- Shortcuts screen — game version from EXE (PEParser — VS_VERSION_INFO, 12 metadata fields), green version badge, "About game" dialog, playtime and launch count on cards
- Steam library redesign — Downloads/Steam tabs, Grid/Compact/Rows views, auto accents and initials on covers, new download cards (percent/speed/ETA), animated buttons
- FPS counter — added display styles (Winlator Ludashi and GameNative)
- FPS limit via WinNative PresentExtension implementation instead of MangoHud — pacer with back-pressure, "PresentPacer"
- LSFG: some minor changes
- Effects: removed the FSR effect
- SensorReader: added new paths
- LSFG frame generation moved in-tree (`cpp/winlator/lsfg/` + DXBC): external `lsfg-vk-android` tree removed, `LsfgVkManager` replaced by `LsfgNative`
- LSFG HUD shows real→shown FPS pair with live armed state
- LSFG: SPIR-V cache pre-built on DLL import, apply without restart

# Shortened changelog

The project license has been changed to **GPLv3**.

### Emulation Core
* Add D7VK 2.3 as a DirectX 1-7 emulation option

### Store Changes
* Improved handling of installed games

### Updated UI
* Added container export/import and download support

* Guided tour

* Unified several screens for improved usability

### XR Input
* 5DoF immersive mode using gamepad mapping

* Added relative mouse support

### XR Support
* Added 360° environment and edge glow effect

* Allow passthrough in immersive mode
* Compositor layer sharpening

* Opentrack advanced menu

# Credits
* **PCVR support** was originally started by **@bigelod**, with the implementation brought to completion by **@lvonasek**. **@GmoLargey** further expanded game compatibility, helping make PCVR support work across a wider range of titles.

* **WinlatorXR development** was largely driven by **@GmoLargey**, with **@lvonasek** taking the project through extensive polishing. **@Gilleece** also contributed additional features and improvements, helping further expand the capabilities of WinlatorXR.
